As a sequitur, the continuation of the reassessment proceedings by the second respondent, who is the jurisdictional Assessing Officer, without issuing any fresh notice as contemplated under section 148, but issuing notice dated 14-12-2018 under section 143(2) read with section 129, which applies only for change in incumbent within the same jurisdiction, is also held to be invalid.[Para 14]

Pertinently, it is to be pointed out at this stage that 'if an order is passed by a judicial or quasi-judicial authority having no jurisdiction, it is an obligation of Appellate Court to rectify the error and set aside the order passed by the authority or forum having no jurisdiction'. Therefore, the notice issued by the first respondent under section 148 as well as the consequential notice issued by the second respondent under section 143(2) read with section 129, cannot be allowed to be sustained. However, the Judge erred in directing the second respondent to continue the reassessment proceedings and granting liberty to the appellant to file objections and avail the opportunity of personal hearing to be provided, by the order impugned herein, which is liable to be set aside, in the considered view of instant court.[Para 15]

As already held by instant court, the first respondent, who recorded the reasons for reopening the assessment under section 148(2), has no jurisdiction over the appellant, to issue notice dated 28-3-2018 under section 148(1). Though the files pertaining to the reassessment proceedings of the appellant were transferred, the second respondent has no authority to continue the reassessment proceedings under section 129 and hence, the notice dated 14-12-2018 issued by him is also held to be invalid. The invalid notices so issued by the respondents vitiate the entire reassessment proceedings initiated against the appellant. Admittedly, no notice under section 148 was issued by the second respondent, who is the jurisdictional Assessing Officer, for reassessment of the return of income of the appellant, within the time frame stipulated under the Act. In this case, the limitation period of six years for reopening the assessment for the year 2011-12 under section 147, came to an end on 31-3-2018. In such circumstances, there is no requirement for instant court to go into the other issue based on the factual matrix projected by the appellant i.e., whether the appellant has disclosed fully and truly all the material particulars that are necessary for assessment for the relevant assessment year.[Para 16]

In the ultimate analysis, the writ appeal stands allowed by setting aside the notices impugned in the writ petition and the order impugned herein.[Para 17]

HEADNOTE: II. Section 148, read with sections 142(1) and 147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for - Assessment year 1997-98 - For assessment year 1997-98, Assessing Officer, on 24-8-1998, issued notice to assessee under section 142(1) - Assessee filed his return on 16-2-2000 - As return filed by assessee was beyond time limit prescribed under section 139(4), i.e., on or before 31-3-1999, Assessing Officer initiated reassessment proceedings against assessee under section 147 and completed assessment - Whether since in instant case revenue had not issued any notice under section 142(1) before end of assessment year and return furnished by assessee under section 139(4) on 16-2-2000 had been filed beyond time-limit prescribed under section 139(4) and was invalid return, in such circumstances, notice under section 148 had to be issued when an assessment, reassessment or recomputation was to be made under section 147 to tax income which had escaped assessment - Held, yes - Whether therefore, assessment completed without issuing notice under section 148 was invalid and bad in law - Held, yes

FACT: For the assessment year 1997-98, the Assessing Officer, on 24-8-1998, issued notice to assessee under section 142(1). The assessee filed his return on 16-2-2000. As the return filed by assessee was beyond time-limit prescribed under section 139(4), i.e., on or before 31-3-1999, the Assessing Officer initiated reassessment proceedings against the assessee under section 147 and completed the assessment. The assessee filed the instant miscellaneous application and contended that no notice under section 148 was ever issued before passing the assessment order. Hence, the assessment under section 147 became invalid.

HELD: No return had been filed by the assessee as per the provisions of the Act and the so-called return filed beyond the time-limit prescribed under section 139(4) on 16-2-2000 was an invalid and non est return in the eyes of law. The proceedings to fasten liability on the assessee-company was commenced by the department for the assessment year 1997-98 by issue of a notice under section 142(1) dated 24-8-1998 for the first time. Prior to it, no notice or proceeding had started. Subsequently, several notices had been issued by the department under section 142(1) but all these notices were apparently issued after the end of the assessment year, i.e., 31-3-1998. As per the provisions of section 147, the income would be treated as escaped assessment at the end of the assessment year where no return had been filed. In the instant case, in the absence of return, the provisions were to tax income that escaped assessment and not to tax income which was not assessed as on 1-4-1998. Thus, the income could be assessed only by issuance of notice under section 148 and in the instant case, no such notice had been issued by the department under section 148. Mere issuance of notice under section 142(1) after the end of the assessment year in the absence of voluntary return by the assessee could not give rise to valid proceedings under the Act.

HEADNOTE: Section 148, read with section 147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Notice of - Assessment years 1971-72 and 1972-73 - Whether, where a valid notice under section 148 had been issued but no assessment had been completed nor were proceedings dropped by the Assessing Officer, he was disentitled to initiate fresh assessment proceedings by issuing another notice under section 148 - Held, yes - Whether assessment completed on the basis of second notice under section 148 would be invalid - Held, yes - Whether, where assessment proceedings initiated on the basis of first notice under section 148 got barred by limitation, they could be revived by issuing fresh notice under section 148 - Held, no

FACT: For the assessment years 1971-72 and 1972-73, notices under section 148 were issued to the assessee-firm. These notices were served on 9-10-1973 on the Receiver who was appointed on 28-7-1972 on a suit for rendition of accounts filed by one of the partners 'V'. No assessment order was passed on the basis of these notices. Thereafter, another set of notices under section 148 was issued for both the assessment years on 31-3-1980 and 17-3-1981. respectively. The assessment for the assessment year 1971-72 was completed ex parte under section 144 on 29-3-1984 while, for the assessment year 1972-73, the assessment was completed under section 143(3) on 20-2-1985. On appeal, the assessee contended before the first appellate authority that assessments had become time-barred as they could not have been framed on the aforesaid dates on the basis of first set of notices issued on 9-10-1973. The appellate authority took the view that perusal of record did not reveal that any notice under section 148 had been issued on 9-10-1973 and the photocopy of the notices produced did not give reasons for initiating the proceedings. Therefore, it was held that the initiation of proceedings under section 148 vide subsequent notices as valid. However, the assessments were set aside for further examination and for fresh assessments.

On second appeal:

HELD: Once notices under section 148 have been issued, the proceedings initiated through them have to be taken to their logical end. In other words, either assessments should be framed on the basis of those proceedings or the Assessing Officer may specifically drop the proceedings, may be on the ground that no sufficient material was available for holding that income liable to tax had escaped assessment. Even if an assessee does not comply with those notices by fling the income-tax returns, the remedy which is open to the revenue is not to issue fresh notices under section 148 but to issue notices under section 142(1) or to have completed the assessments under section 144. Thus, if the assessments have got barred by limitation, they cannot be revived by issuing fresh notices. In the instant case, this position was clear to the Assessing Officer and other officers of the department as could be gathered from a DO letter written by ITO to his IAC in which he had written that in this case, the assessment for the assessment year 1972-73 had been completed on a total income of Rs. 2,53,400 on 20-2-1985 as a result of which a demand was created. He had further written that the assessment was completed in pursuance of action initiated under section 148 subsequent to an action under section 148 got time- barred. He had further mentioned that this matter was discussed with the Commissioner and that according to the Commissioner the demand was unrealisable and assessment was likely to be annulled.

In the circumstances, it was to be held that since in the instant case valid Notices for the assessment years under consideration had been issued by The Assessing Officer on 9-10-1973 but he failed to complete the assessments within the time allowed under law, the assessments got barred by time for both the years. Further, the assessments dated 29-3-1984 for the assessment year 1971-72 and 20-2-1985 for the assessment year 1972-73 were invalid, because they were completed on the basis of fresh notices issued under section 148 dated 31-3-1980 and 17-3-1981, i.e., at a time when the original proceedings initiated under section 148 were still pending.

Hence, both the assessments framed by the Assessing Officer for those two assessment years had to be annulled.

HEADNOTE: Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Notice of - Assessment year 1961-62 - Whether issuance of notice within period of limitation gives jurisdiction to Assessing Officer to proceed to make reassessment irrespective of whether or not it is served within period of limitation - Held, yes

FACT: For the assessment year 1961-62, a notice under section 148 was issued and despatched on 24-2-1970. No return was filed in response thereto. Therefore, the Assessing Officer issued another notice on 10-10-1973 under section 142(1) intimating to the assessee to appear on 23-11-1973. The assessee filed a reply to this notice stating that the alleged notice under section 148 was not served upon him and no proceedings under section 148 could be maintained against him as notice was not served upon him within 8 years. However, on 13-5-1974, an assessment order under section 144 was passed. By filing writ petition the assessee challenged the reassessment order. The High Court held that notice issued before limitation, if served on the assessee after limitation, would be void and ineffective but since an appeal was pending against the order of assessment, the High Court directed that the appeal be decided by the appellate authority in accordance with law.

On appeal to the Supreme Court:

HELD: The point of law involved for decision was already settled in R.K. Upadhyaya v. Shanabhai P. Patel [1987] 166 ITR 163 in which it had been held that the issuance of notice within the period of limitation gives jurisdiction to the Assessing Officer to make reassessment. It appeared that the High Court directed the AAC to decide the assessee's appeal in accordance with law and in doing so to also ascertain when the notice under section 148 had been despatched by registered post. There was, thus, no occasion to interfere with the order made by the High Court.

FACT: ■

The assessee filed his return of income for assessment year 2015-16 on 17-9-2015 declaring total income of Rs. 11.87 crores. Subsequently, the case was taken up for reassessment proceedings based on the information received under Risk Management Strategy as formulated by the CBDT.

■

Notice under section 148 dated 23-6-2021 was issued after obtaining the prior approval of the PCIT.

The Assessing Officer vide order under section 147 read with section 144B dated 29-5-2023 completed the assessment at income of Rs. 36.25 crores by disallowing the short term capital loss under section 94(7) and adding the said amount.

HELD: ■

From perusal of the records, it reveals that it is an undisputed fact that the year under consideration is relating to assessment year 2015-16, and accordingly, the limitation period available to the Assessing Officer for issuance of notice under section 148, as per section 149, was expired on 31-3-2022. However, the notice under section 148 was issued on 29-7-2022, thus, the issuance of notice under section 148 on 29-7-2022 is barred by limitation. Consequently, the reassessment proceedings culminating in the order under section 147 read with section 144B are rendered void ab initio, having been initiated beyond the prescribed statutory period and lacking legal sustainability. In view of the aforesaid, the impugned order dated 29-7-2022 issued under section 148(A)(d) as well as the notice dated 29-7-2022 issued under section 148 in respect of assessment year 2015-16 deserve to be quashed. [Para 5.2]

■

It is further noted that even otherwise, the limitation period must be strictly construed in accordance with the statutory provisions of the Act as amended by the Finance Act, 2021, read with TOLA and judicial pronouncements of the Supreme Court.[Para 5.3]

■

Under the provisions of section 149 as applicable at the relevant time, the outer limitation for reopening AY 2008-09 expired on 31.03.2015. Thus, the notice issued under section 148 is admittedly time-barred. [Para 9.8]

■ The question then arises as to the point of time at which limitation is required to be examined under section 150(2). This issue is no longer res integra. The Jaipur Bench of the Tribunal in the case of Ramesh Chand Soni (HUF) v. ITO [2018] 89 taxmann.com 71 (Jaipur - Trib.) after considering the provisions of section 150(2) and the decision of the Hon'ble Kerala High Court in CIT v. Vaikundom Rubber Co. Ltd. [2001] 114 Taxman 378/249 ITR 19 (Kerala) held that where the Tribunal passes a finding or direction in second appeal, the relevant date for examining limitation under section 150(2) is not the date of the Tribunal order but the date of the order which was the subject matter of appeal before the Tribunal, namely the order of the CIT(A). The Tribunal categorically held that limitation under section 149 has to be reckoned up to the date of the appellate order which was under challenge before the Tribunal. [Para 9.9]

■

Respectfully following Ramesh Chand Soni (HUF) (supra), it is held that for the purposes of section 150(2), the relevant date in the present case is the date of the CIT(A)'s order for AY 2007-08, which was the subject matter of appeal before the Tribunal. [Para 9.10]

■

In the present case, the CIT(A) passed the order for AY 2007-08 on 02.02.2017. By that date, the limitation for reopening AY 2008-09 under section 149 had already expired on 31.03.2015. Therefore, on the date when the order which formed the subject matter of appeal before the Tribunal came into existence, the assessment for AY 2008-09 had already become time-barred. [Para 9.11]

■

Section 150(2) expressly provides that section 150(1) shall not apply in such circumstances. The legislative intent is clear. Section 150 cannot be utilised as a mechanism to revive a dead assessment or to reopen an assessment which had already become barred by limitation on the relevant date. The provision only saves those cases where the assessment was still alive and capable of being reopened on the date contemplated under section 150(2). Therefore, even assuming for the sake of argument that the Tribunal order contained a finding or direction, the Revenue would still be confronted with the statutory bar contained in section 150(2). Since the limitation for reopening AY 2008-09 had expired on 31.03.2015 and no time was available on 02.02.2017, the extended jurisdiction contemplated under section 150(1) stood expressly excluded by operation of section 150(2). [Para 9.12]

■

In view of the foregoing discussion, it is held that the Tribunal order for AY 2007-08 did not contain any finding or direction within the meaning of section 150(1). Consequently, invocation of section 150(1) by the AO for reopening AY 2008-09 was without jurisdiction. Even otherwise, the reopening is independently barred by section 150(2) since the limitation prescribed under section 149 had already expired on 31.03.2015 and no valid reassessment could have been made on the date of the CIT(A)'s order dated 02.02.2017, which was the order forming the subject matter of appeal before the Tribunal. Therefore, the notice issued under section 148 dated 19.03.2018 and the consequential reassessment framed pursuant thereto are void ab initio, barred by limitation and unsustainable in law. Accordingly, the notice issued under section 148 as well as the consequential reassessment order are quashed. Since the legal grounds challenging the assumption of jurisdiction itself have been allowed, the other grounds raised on merits become academic and do not call for adjudication. Hence, the legal grounds raised by the assessee are allowed. [Para 9.13]

Therefore, in the considered view of the Tribunal, in light of the first proviso to section 149 of the Act, the A.O. could not have issued notice under section 148 of the Act, after 31.03.2022 for the assessment year 2015-16. ■ The Tribunal further finds that, although the Revenue has contended that as per the amended provisions of section 149 of the Act, where income escaping assessment exceeds Rs.50,00,000/-, the time limit for issuance of notice under section 148 of the Act, has been extended up to ten years, such extended time limit cannot be applied to cases where the limitation under the old regime had already expired. In the present case, since the limitation for issuance of notice under section 148 of the Act, had already expired on 31.03.2022, in the considered view of the Tribunal, the notice issued by the A.O. under section 148 of the Act, dated 23.04.2022 is barred by limitation and consequently the assessment order passed by the A.O. under section 147 r.w.s. 144 r.w.s. 144B of the Act, is bad in law and liable to be quashed. Since the reassessment proceedings have been quashed on the legal issue, the other grounds raised by the assessee on merits become academic in nature and are not adjudicated. [Para 10]

HEADNOTE: Section  148,  read with sections  147,  144  and  144B, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Issue of notice for  (Limitation) - Assessment year  2015-16  - Whether notice under section 148 issued on 23-4-2022 for assessment year 2015-16, being issued after 1-4-2021, was beyond limitation and therefore without jurisdiction - Held, yes - Whether consequently reassessment order, demand notice, penalty notices/orders and recovery notices were to be quashed - Held, yes [Paras 6 and 11] [In favour of assessee]

FACT: ■

The Assessing Officer issued a notice under section 148 dated 23-4-2022 for assessment year 2015-16 and thereafter passed a reassessment order dated 11-3-2024 under section 147 read with sections 144 and 144B, issued a demand notice under section 156, initiated penalty proceedings, and commenced recovery action, threatening the petitioner with coercive steps.

■

The petitioner filed a writ petition before the High Court seeking to quash the notice issued under section 148 and all consequential proceedings, including the reassessment order, demand notice, and penalty notices/orders, contending that the notice was barred by limitation as it was issued after 1-4-2021 and therefore was without jurisdiction.

■

It was submitted that an appeal against the reassessment order had already been filed before the Commissioner (Appeals) and was pending, and the petitioner undertook to withdraw the appeal if the writ petition was allowed.

HELD: ■

It is not in dispute that the present petition relates to assessment year 2015-16. Further, it is also undisputed that the notice under section 148 has been issued on 23-4-2022. [Para 6]

■

From the judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of UOI v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70 /301 Taxman 238/469 ITR 46 (SC) it is clear, that the department has conceded before the Supreme Court that all the notices issued under section 148 after 1-4-2021 for assessment year 2015-16 have to be dropped. In the present case, the notice under section 148 is dated 23-4-2022 and therefore, has to be dropped. [Para 7]

■

The decision in Rajeev Bansal (supra) has been subsequently followed by the Supreme Court in Deepak Steel and Power Ltd. v. CBDT [2025] 174 taxmann.com 144/305 Taxman 169/476 ITR 369 (SC). [Para 8]

■

Similarly, even in the matter of Asstt. CIT v. Nehal Ashit Shah [SLP (Civil) Diary No.(S) 57209/2024, dated 4-4-2025], the Supreme Court, relying upon paragraphs 19(e) and (f) of the decision in case of Rajeev Bansal (supra), dismissed the SLP filed by the revenue. [Para 9]

■

Lastly, this very Bench on 6-10-2025, in the matter of Verjinia Foods Ltd. v. ITO [2025] 179 taxmann.com 626/307 Taxman 563 (Bombay), has allowed the petition filed by the Petitioner therein by noting that since the notice under section 148 was issued after 1-4-2021, the same was required to be set aside in light of the concession made by the revenue before the Supreme Court in the case of Rajeev Bansal (supra). [Para 10]

■

In light of the above discussion, there is merit in the submissions as canvassed by the assessee. The revenue has categorically made a concession that for assessment year 2015-16 they would drop all notices issued under section 148 after 1-4-2021. Once this is the position, it is appropriate that the notice under section 148 dated 23-4-2022, and the consequential assessment order, notice of demand, penalty notices/orders as well as the recovery notices be quashed and set aside. It is accordingly so ordered. [Para 11]

■ Now, with respect to the appeal by the revenue and cross objection by the assessee for assessment year 2015-16. Appeal by the revenue is on the merits of the case whereas cross objection by the assessee is on challenging the legal issue of notice under section 148 as bad in law, invalid, void ab initio, to be quashed. Accordingly, the legal issue raised by the assessee through its cross objection is taken up as it goes to the root of the matter. [Para 11]

■

Identical chronology of events exists for assessment year 2015-16 as discussed while adjudicating appeal for assessment year 2014-15 in the above paragraphs, except for date of filing of return. Notice under section 148 of the old regime was issued on 30-6-2021. Later, pursuant to the judgment in case of Ashish Agarwal (supra), it was directed among other things that notice issued under section 148 shall be deemed to have been issued under section 148A as substituted by the Finance Act, 2021 and construed or treated to be the show cause notice in terms of section 148A(b). In view of this direction, the said notice under section 148, dated 30-6-2021 was deemed to be a show cause notice under section 148A(b) for which another one was issued on 26-5-2022, complying with the direction given in the case of Ashish Agarwal (supra). [Para 12]

■

Thereafter, provisions of section 148A(d) were complied with by passing an order, dated 28-7-2022 and issuing a notice under section 148 of the same date (under the new regime). Assessee has contested by raising a ground of cross objection that the notice so issued is bad in law, invalid, void ab initio, to be quashed. The assessee strongly submitted that it is barred by limitation making the impugned reassessment proceedings and resultant reassessment order bad in law. [Para 12.1]

■

At the outset, it is found that this issue has been settled in the case of Rajeev Bansal (supra) wherein reference is made to the submissions made on behalf of the revenue which is relevant. [Para 12.2]

■

Thus, it can be seen that revenue conceded before the Supreme Court for dropping all the notices issued on or after 1-4-2021 for assessment year 2015-16 as they will not fall for completion during the period prescribed under TOLA. [Para 12.3]

■

In the case of present assessee, since the notice issued under section 148 is dated 28-7-2022, period of six years expired on 31-3-2022 and is thus barred by limitation. Accordingly, notice so issued and re-assessment completed thereafter under section 147 is liable to be quashed, in view of the decision of Supreme Court in the case of Rajeev Bansal (supra). [Para 12.5]

■

In view of above stated deliberation, both on facts and law including the applicable jurisprudence, it is held that notice for assessment year 2015-16 issued on 28-7-2022 under section 148 of the new regime is barred by limitation and hence bad in law, liable to be quashed, resulting in impugned reassessment proceedings as well as the impugned reassessment order bad in law. Accordingly, grounds of cross objection raised by the assessee are allowed. Resultantly, grounds of appeal raised on the merits of the case by the revenue are rendered academic and are therefore, dismissed. [Para 12.7]

■

In the result, for assessment year 2015-16, appeal by the revenue is dismissed and cross objection by the assessee is allowed. For assessment year 2014-15, appeal by the revenue is dismissed. [Para 13]

or order of the appellate authority or revision authority then the limitation provided under section 149 would not be applicable. However, the said extension of time limit under section 150(1) is also not absolute but is subject to the condition and restrictions as envisaged in sub-section (2) of section 150. Further, section 151 contemplates requirement of sanction where the notice under section 148 is issued after expiry of four years from the end of the assessment year. [Para 5] The plain reading of these provisions of section 149 to 151 reveals that section 150(1) provides exception to the limitation provided under section 149 for issuing notice under section 148. Therefore, section 150 can be pressed into service in a particular case of reopening based on the directions or giving effect to the order of the appellate authority only when the time limitation provided under section 149 has already expired. In the case in hand, the time limit provided under section 149 was certainly not expired as on 31-4-2011, however, it is certainly after the expiry of four years from the end of the assessment year and, therefore, as per the provisions of section 151, the notice under section 148 cannot be issued unless the Principal Chief Commissioner, Chief Commissioner, Principal Commissioner or Commissioner is satisfied on the reasons recorded by the Assessing Officer that it is a fit case for issue of such notice. Therefore, the condition set out in section 151 and particularly in the proviso to section 150(1) as existed at relevant time is a mandatory condition for issuing notice under section 148. If such notice is issued after expiry of four years from end of the relevant assessment year section 151 gives jurisdiction to the Assessing Officer to initiate the proceedings under section 147 and in absence of the sanction of the authority provided under section 151, the notice issued by the Assessing Officer is invalid. The provisions of section 150 is only an exception to the limitation provided under section 149 and, therefore, the said section cannot be taken as an exception to section 151. Hence, even if the assessment is reopened to make reassessment in consequence of or to give effect to any finding or direction of the appellate authority the requirement of sanction under section 151 is mandatory for issuing notice under section 147. Even otherwise from the plain reading of section 150(1), it is clear that it begins with non-obstante clause as far as the limitation provided under section 149 and, therefore, section 150(1) has an overriding effect on section 149 and not over section 151. The requirement of sanction under section 151 is in the nature of check and balance and it is a measure against the misuse of power by the assessing authority for assessment or reassessment based the reasons not found satisfactory by the authorities provided under section 151. Accordingly, when the Assessing Officer admittedly issued notice under section 148 after the four years from the end of the assessment year and without obtaining the sanction under section 151 then such notice issued under section 148 is in violation of provisions of section 151 and, consequently, the same was invalid and the entire reassessment proceedings stand vitiated. Hence, the reopening of the assessee is not valid and the same is quashed. The consequential reassessment is also quashed. [Para 5]

FACT: For the assessment year 1987-88, the assessee’s return of income was due to be filed on 31-7-1987, but it was not filed even till 25-10-1988, when a notice under section 148 was issued. In response to the said notice, the assessee filed its return on 30-3-1989, and the assessment was completed on 22-8-1990 under section 143(3) read with section 147(a). The assessee appealed against the assessment order contending that the assessment officer was not competent to issue the notice under section 148 until the limitation for filing the return under section 139(4) expired and as such the return filed on 30-3-1989. even after the service of notice under section 148, was to be treated as a return under section 139(4) and the notice under section 148 was non est in law. The Commissioner (Appeals) held that as there was no valid return before the notice was issued, the notice under section 148 was valid and upheld the assessment order.

On second appeal, the assessee reiterating its earlier arguments, contended (i) that the notice under section 148 was invalid; and (ii) that the return filed in response to such notice was to be treated as a return under section 139(4), and hence, the assessment completed on 22-8-1990 was barred by limitation.

HELD: As regards the validity of notice issued under section 148, the first condition laid down in section 148(1) for issuance of notice is that it should be issued before making assessment, re-assessment and re-computation of income. In the instant case, the notice under section 148 was issued on 25-10-1988 and the assessment was completed on 22-8-1990. Thus, the notice issued under section 148 was valid as it was issued before the assessment was made. Then, according to the provisions envisaged and limitation laid down in section 149(1), no notice under section 148 would be issued in cases falling under clause (a) of section 147 for the relevant assessment year if eight years had elapsed from the end of that year. In the instant case, the relevant assessment year was 1987-88 and 8 years from the end of that year would elapse in 1996. But the notice under section 148 was already issued on 25-10-1988 and was, therefore, well within the prescribed time limit of eight years, i.e., before 31-3-1990. The assessee’s contention that the notice under section 148 issued prior to 31-3-1990 could not take the right of the assessee to file the return under section 139(4) was also not tenable as, in the instant case, no return was furnished before the issuance of notice under section 148. Moreover, there was no provision in the Act to invalidate the notice under section 148 by furnishing of return after the issue of such notice.

On writ to the High Court: HELD: At the outset it requires to be noted that the effect of the order passed by this Court on 20-2-2013 was that the VBPPL (which was one of the transferor companies) amalgamated with the petitioner with effect from 1-4-2012. Therefore, by operation of law, VBPPL ceased to exist with effect from 1-4-2012. The fact that the order of the High Court may have been passed only on 20-2-2013, and that the Department became aware of that fact even later, will not make any difference to the legal position. [Para 19]

Any notices to the transferor company (which included VBPPL) that may be issued thereafter would be responded to by the Petitioner. This is not be understood to mean that proceedings initiated against any of the transferor companies, including VBPPL, by the Department prior to that date would be continued against the petitioner. What it meant was that notices issued thereafter to VBPPL after it ceased to exist would be responded to by the petitioner. That condition has been complied with since in fact the petitioner answered the notices issued to VBPPL after 1-4-2012. [Para 20]

The resultant position is that on 3-4-2012 when the notice under section 148 was issued to VBPPL, it was issued to an entity which was non-existent in the eye of law. [Para 21]

In the present case not only was the initial notice under section 148 issued to a non-existent entity even the search under section 153A took place against a non-existent entity. Both the warrant of authorisation and the panchnama were drawn in the name of VBPPL on 3-1-2014 by which date even the order of the High Court approving the amalgamation of the VBPPL with the Petitioner had been passed. Clearly, therefore, the entire proceedings under section 153A were void ab initio. Therefore, the question of invoking section 153A(2) to revive the abated re-assessment proceedings under section 147/148 did not arise.[Para 23]

It requires reiteration that the proceedings under section 148 which commenced with the notice dated 3-4-2012 issued to VBPPL were itself void ab initio for the simple reason that on that day VBPPL was not in existence as a result of the order dated 20-2-2013 of the High Court approving its amalgamation with the petitioner with effect from 1-4-2012. The question of revival of such proceedings at a later point in time, with there being no change to the legal position regarding VBPPL having ceased to exist, does not arise. The mere fact that prior to 20-2-2013 (being the date of the order approving the amalgamation) VBPPL and/or the petitioner may have responded to such notices, will not make a difference to the said legal position. The facts show that after 20-2-2013, the petitioner lost no opportunity in reminding the Assessing Officer at every stage that VBPPL no longer existed in the eye of law. Despite being made aware of this legal position, the Assessing Officer persisted in continuing the proceedings against VBPPL. [Para 24]

The reassessment proceedings under section 147 were barred by limitation since limitation for framing the assessment under section 143(3) read with section 147 expired on 31-3-2014. On this ground also, the question of revival of those proceedings by the impugned letter dated 14-3-2016 was bad in law.[Para 25]

The notice dated 3-4-2012 and the letter 14-3-2016 issued by the Assessing Officer under section 148 seeking to reopen the assessment of the assessee for the assessment year in question is to be quashed. [Para 26]

Sub-section (2) excludes the applicability of sub-section (1) in certain circumstances enumerated therein. [Para 37]

From a perusal of section 151 the following propositions emerge :— (i )if an assessment has been made under sub-section (3) of section 143 or section 147 and four years have not expired from the end of the relevant assessment year, a notice under section 148 has to be issued by the Assessing Officer who is not below the rank of the Assistant Commissioner or the Joint Commissioner but before issuing any such notice, the Joint Commissioner is to be satisfied with the reasons recorded by such Assessing Officer that it is a fit case for issue of such notice. Here ‘Joint Commissioner’, would also include an Additional Commissioner, in view of the definition of the phrase ‘Joint Commissioner’ as contained in section 2(28C). The satisfaction has to be necessarily recorded by the Additional Commissioner or the Joint Commissioner, as the case may be. However, if the Assessing Officer is the Additional Commissioner or the Joint Commissioner, then in that case prior approval of any higher officer is not required in case he has recorded the reasons for issuing notice in view of the provisions of sub-sections (4) and (5) of section 120;

(ii )if, however, the period of four years has expired and the assessment order has been made under sub-section (3) of section 143 or section 147, the notice is to be issued only after the satisfaction has been recorded by either the Chief Commissioner or the Commissioner about the reasons recorded by the Assessing Officer that it is a fit case for issue of such notice. Thus, the Assessing Officer not below the rank of the Assistant Commissioner can issue a notice but before issuing the notice, the satisfaction of the Commissioner or the Chief Commissioner of the Income-tax is necessarily to be obtained. This would be the position after 1-4-1988 in view of the omission of the words ‘Additional Commissioner’ in section 2(16) by the Direct Tax Laws (Amendment) Act, 1987; and

(iii )where an assessment has not been made under sub-section (3) of section 143 or section 147 and the period of four years from the end of the relevant assessment year has expired, notice under section 148 can be issued only by an officer of the rank of the Joint Commissioner after being satisfied with the reasons recorded by the Assessing Officer that it is a fit case for issue of such notice. Here, the term ‘Joint Commissioner’ is inter-changeable with the words ‘Additional Commissioner’ in view of the definition of the term ‘Joint Commissioner’, as given in section 2(28C). [Para 39]

In view of the various provisions of the Act defining jurisdiction of the various authorities and the powers, procedure to be adopted and the limitations imposed upon such authorities for making assessment or reassessment, it is clear that if under the provisions of the Act an authority is required to exercise powers or to do an act in a particular manner, then that power has to be exercised and the act has to be performed in that manner alone and not in any other manner. [Para 40]

Thus, if the assessment has been made under sub-section (3) of section 143 or section 147 and the proceedings for reassessment are to be initiated after a period of four years, then the notice can be issued only after the Chief Commissioner or Commissioner of Income-tax, as the case may be, has recorded his satisfaction, for issuance of notice as provided under the proviso to sub-section (1) of section 151. [Para 41]

It is well-settled that a notice issued without obtaining the prior sanction of the authority mentioned in the provisions of section 151, whether it is the proviso to sub-section (1) or sub-section (2), would be, invalid and the entire proceeding taken in pursuance thereof is liable to be quashed as the same would be without jurisdiction. [Para 51]

Applying the principles laid down to the facts of the instant case, there was no dispute between the parties that the impugned notices dated 12-9-2000 had been issued without obtaining the prior sanction of the Chief Commissioner or the Commissioner of Income-tax which was obligatory on the part of the Assessing Officer, as in all those assessment years, assessment/reassessment had been completed under sub-section (3) of section 143 or section 147 and the notice under section 148, dated 12-9-2000 had been issued much after the expiry of the period of four years from the end of the relevant assessment years. Thus, the impugned notices were invalid, could not be sustained and were hereby set aside. Consequently, all proceedings taken in pursuance of those notices were also set aside. [Para 52]

In view of the discussions, all the writ petitions succeeded and were allowed.

HEADNOTE: Section 147, read with section 142(1), of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - General - Assessment year 1991-92 - Whether, where assessee failed to file its return suo moto and Assessing Officer failed to issue a notice under section 142(1) during relevant assessment year, then it would be a case of escaped assessment and, therefore, a notice under section 148 is compulsory to proceed with assessment - Held, yes

Section 142(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Assessment - Enquiry before - Whether, even though no time limit has been explicitly prescribed for issue of notice under section 142(1), such limit of issuing notice within relevant assessment year is built into section under scheme of Act - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, where relevant assessment year expired on 31-3-1992, notices under section 142(1) issued by Assessing Officer thereafter on 26-5-1992 and 28-5-1993 were invalid and assessments completed in pursuance thereof were invalid in law - Held, yes

FACT: For the assessment year 1991-92, the assessees did not file their returns under section 139 either voluntarily before the due dates or after the issue of notices under section 142(1)(1) by the Assessing Officer on 26-5-1992. Therefore, again notices were issued under section 142(1)(i) on 28-5-1993 to the assessees, where after returns were filed on 22-12-1993. As the returns were filed beyond one year from the end of the assessment year, i.e., 31-3-1991, the Assessing Officer treated the returns as invalid and, therefore, completed the assessments under section 144.

On second appeal, the assessees submitted that it was a case of income escaping assessment and, therefore, the initiation of assessment proceedings without issuing a notice under section 148 was invalid. Further, the assessee contended that as the notice under section 142(1) is a substitution of the requirement under section 139(2), the time limit for its issuance within the assessment year was in built.

On the other hand, the revenue argued that the notice under section 142(1)( i) could be issued at any time after the assessee’s failure to file a return under section 139 and that since action for filing the return had already been initiated by issue of a notice under section 142(1)(i), the provisions of section 148 would not come into play and the consequences of filing or non-filing of return in pursuance thereof would follow. The revenue also contended that since the assessee had filed the returns of income in pursuance of notices under section 142(1)(i) it would not be a case of income escaping assessment within the meaning of Explanation 2( a) to section 147. It was also submitted that the proceedings for assessment had been initiated within two years from the end of assessment year as prescribed under section 153(1)(a) and, therefore, there was no necessity to issue a notice under section 148.

HELD: A notice under section 148 has to be issued when an assessment, reassessment or recomputation is made under section 147 to tax income which has escaped assessment. The instant case was not a case of reassessment nor a case of recomputation. It was a case of an assessment without there being an earlier assessment.

Under the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, originally there was no time limit for completion of assessment until the amendment made in 1939 and Courts have held that the notice under section 34 was not required to be served if the proceedings were pending on either the assessee filing the return suo moto or by issuance of notice under section 22 (equivalent to section 142 of the Income-tax Act. 1961). After the introduction of the time limit for completing the assessments under the Income-tax Act, 1961, the proceedings could be said to be pending during the period starting from the date of filing of the return by the assessee suo moto or issuance of notice under section 142 by the Assessing Officer up to the lime limit prescribed to complete the assessment under section 153, i.e., two years from the end of the assessment year in which the income was first assessable.

FACT: The Assessing Officer completed the assessment of the assessee. Subsequently, the Assessing Officer issued notice on 31-3-2005 under section 148 for re-opening of assessment of the assessee. The assessee challenged proceedings under section 147, by filing a writ petition before the High Court whereby the High Court passed an interim order dated 6-1-2006. Later on interim relief so granted was extended up to 9-2-2007. Thereafter, the Assessing Officer passed reassessment order on 31-12-2008. On revenue’s appeal :

HELD: The Commissioner (Appeals) had correctly held the order dated 31-12-2008 passed under section 147/143(3) as barred by limitation. Admittedly, the notice under section 148 was served upon the assessee on 31-3-2005 and therefore, the time-limit available for completion of assessment in pursuance thereof was due to expire by 31-3-2006. The Commissioner (Appeals) had correctly observed that the period from 6-1-2006 to 9-2-2007 was to be excluded from the computation of ‘time-limit’ as per Explanation 1 below sub-section (4) of section 153. It was observed that there were interim orders dated 6-1-2006 and 12-1-2007 to the effect that the Assessing Officer would not pass the final order. Admittedly, the interim order granted by the High Court was in force up to 9-2-2007. Thereafter, there was no extension of interim relief. In view of the above, the time-limit for passing the assessment order expired on 6-5-2007. Therefore, the order passed by the Assessing Officer on 31-12-2008 was clearly barred by limitation. Accordingly, the order of the Commissioner (Appeals) was to be confirmed in holding the assessment as invalid.

149 is lifted up and as per section 150(1) notice under section 148 could be issued at any time. Therefore, it is necessary to understand the definition and meaning of 'finding' or 'direction'. If in this case of the assessee, the basis on which notice under section 148 issued pertains to any finding or direction, then section 150(1) will apply or else embargo provided under section 149 of the Act will be applicable. [Para 9] Therefore, it is absolutely clear that the term 'finding' and 'direction' has to be a specific finding and direction. They cannot be incidental; rather finding and direction should be of the case and of the order which is before the authority adjudicating the same. In the case of the assessee, the order passed by the Commissioner (Appeals), dated 28-2-2013 simply says that since the issue before him relates to assessment year 2008-09, there is no liability for capital gain tax during that year. Thereafter, the Commissioner (Appeals) further states that the Assessing Officer may consider computation of capital gains in assessment year 2005-06. Had the word 'may' been used as 'shall', it would have a specific direction or finding. With the word 'may' it is an observation, a plausible view of the Commissioner (Appeals). Having said so, it was found that the assessment year ends on 31-3-2006 and as per section 149, within six years, i.e., maximum within 31-3-2012 notice under section 148 could have been issued. But in the case of the assessee, appellate order itself was passed on 28-2-2013. By the time appellate order was passed, the period of limitation, i.e., 31-3-2012 has already expired.

So far as revenue is concerned, section 150(1) findings and directions which is embedded therein in the case of the assessee that is not applicable since the Commissioner (Appeals) has merely stated his view and opinion. Having said so, in merits embargo enshrined in section 149 is operative and here within six years notice should have been issued but in the case of the assessee, it was not done and the appellate order itself, which is the basis of issue of notice under section 148 and very basis for invoking provisions of section 150(1), was passed on 28-2-2013. Notice under section 148 was issued thereafter, therefore, it is beyond the period of limitation. [Para 11]

The guidance may be taken from the decision of the Apex Court in the case of K.M. Sharma v. ITO [2002] 122 Taxman 426/254 ITR 772 wherein it was held that fiscal statute more particularly on a provision such as the present one regulating period of limitation must receive strict construction. Law of limitation is intended to give certainty and finality to legal proceedings and to avoid exposure to risk of litigation to litigant. Proceedings, which have attained finality under existing law due to bar of limitation cannot be held to be open for revival unless the amended provision is clearly given retrospective operation so as to allow upsetting of proceedings, which had already been concluded and attained finality. The amendment to sub-section (1) of Section 150 is not expressed to be retrospective and, therefore, has to be held as only prospective. The amendment made to sub-section (1) of section 150 which intends to lift embargo of period of limitation under section 149 to enable Authorities to reopen assessments not only on the basis of Orders passed in proceedings under the Act but also on Order of a Court in any proceedings under any law has to be applied prospectively.

Therefore, even as per rule, strict construction and limitation of section 149 applies until and unless ingredients of section 150(1) is fulfilled. In the instant case the ingredients of section 150(1), which the revenue has made the basis for issue of notice under section 148, itself is not satisfied, therefore, issuance of notice under section 148 is directly hit by the provisions of section 149 limitation. Therefore, it is held that since issuance of 148 notice is barred by limitation, serving of notice itself is invalid and bad in law and, therefore, any consequent assessment or reassessment is obviously null and void. Therefore, the order of the Commissioner (Appeals) is set aside and quashing of the reassessment proceedings is directed. [Para 12]

In the result, appeal of the assessee is allowed. [Para 13]

FACT: The assessee was HUF and proprietor of 'T' Ltd. The assessee filed its return of income declaring certain taxable income on 31-3-2003 which was processed under section 143(1). Subsequently the case was reopened under section 147/148 and assessment was completed under section 143(3) read with section 147.

A survey under section 133A was carried out in the business premises of 'T' Ltd. in which the Karta of the assessee HUF was a director. During the survey, a printout of cash book of 'T' Ltd. for the period 1-4-2001 to 28-6-2001 was found. As per the said printout the Assessing Officer of the said company found that there was an excess payment of Rs. 11,44,658/- and accordingly, the addition of the said amount was made in the hands of the company for want of satisfactory explanation. The said addition was confirmed by the Commissioner (Appeals) vide his order dated 15-7-2009.

The Tribunal deleted said addition in the hands of 'T' Ltd. by holding that the said document belongs to 'T' proprietorship of the assessee HUF and the income if any arising from such transactions was held to be assessed in the hands of assessee instead of 'T' Ltd.

Based on the findings of the Tribunal in the case of 'T' Ltd. vide order dated 26-3-2010 the Assessing Officer initiated proceedings under section 147 and issued a notice under section 148 on 30-7-2010.

The assessee filed objections against the initiation of the proceedings under section 148 which was rejected by the Assessing Officer. Thereafter, the Assessing Officer completed the assessment under section 143(3) read with section 147 on 1-12-2011. The assessee challenged the action of the Assessing Officer including the validity of reopening before the Commissioner (Appeals) but could not succeed.

The assessee filed instant appeal submitting that the notice issued under section 148 on 30-7-2010 was barred by limitation as provided under section 149 read with section 150. It was further contended that the notice under section 148 was issued on 30-7-2010 and as per restrictions provided under section 150(2) the time limit prescribed under section 149 had already expired on 31-3-2009. Thus, reassessment proceedings were illegal and void.

HELD: The Assessing Officer proposed to reopen the assessment of the two assessment years i.e. 2001-02 & 2002-03 vide notice under section 148 dated 30-07-2010. Thus, it is apparent that the notice issued under section 148 for initiation of reassessment proceedings is beyond the limitation provided under section 149 as exists at the relevant point of time.

It is clear that no notice under section 148 shall be issued in any case after the expiry of 6 years, however, the limitation provided under section 149 is applicable in a situation where the Assessing Officer on its own on the basis of fresh material or information forms an opinion that the income assessable to tax has escaped assessment. Section 150 provides the assessment or reassessment in pursuant to an order of appeal, revision or reference and therefore, the limitation provided under section 149 for reopening of the assessment is not per se applicable when the reopening is based on the directions of the appellate or revisional authority or as per the directions of the Court.

On appeal : HELD: Section 148 provides provisions for initiation of the reassessment proceedings. The initiation has to be made with the issue of a notice under section 148 on the assessee concerned. In the instant case from the facts alone, the notice for the assessment year 1981-82 was barred by limitation under section 149(1)(a)(ii ) and as such the assessment done in pursuance of time-barred notice was liable to be quashed. Mere acceptance, acquiescence and participation in such a proceeding where notice is served beyond the period of statutory limitation cannot remedy the defect for not issuing the notice within the period of limitation, and that does not confer authority on the Assessing Officer to assume jurisdiction. Service of notice within the statutory period is a sine qua non and is an indispensable requisite for the initiation of assessment proceeding under section 148 where income has escaped assessment. The Assessing Officer, in the instant case, having failed to comply with the statutory requirement, could not assume jurisdiction and as such, the assessment order for the assessment year 1981-82 in the assessment proceedings passed by him pursuant to such time-barred notice for the said assessment year could not be sustained and no appellate authority including the Tribunal could give authority or jurisdiction to the Assessing Officer in such cases, as no life could be given to a dead horse. Further, in all the notices of the assessment years 1982-83 to 1986-87 including the assessment year 1981-82, there was no mention as to the status of the assessee even though the department was aware of the status of the assesee as individual having already assessed the assessee in the said status, i.e., in the ‘individual’ capacity only on salary income.

If the department sought to assess him in the status of ‘oral trust’, the status should have been mentioned in the notice itself. Without mentioning the status in the notice itself, the said notice could not be taken advantage of to start proceedings under section 148 against the ‘oral trust’. Therefore, the assessment for all the years under consideration made pursuant to such invalid notice, must be quashed.

Whatever and howsoever noble may be the purpose of any trust (religious or evangelic), they cannot escape themselves from the responsibility of accountability before the revenue. Otherwise, the very purpose of the existence of the revenue to control the source of funds and expenditures of any person/assessee would be futile.

The primary onus to furnish the accounts to the Income-tax Department like all other law-abiding citizens irrespective of caste, creed, colour, community and religion heavily lies on the person/assessee. In the instant case the assessee as an individual might be receiving salary for the work done by him sincerely on propagation of Christianity but that did not mean that the department would close its eyes to the accounts maintained by him for the funds received from abroad and expenditures thereof.

In the result, the appeals were to be allowed.

The assessee sought that the reopening notice issued after expiry of six years from end of the relevant assessment year was barred by limitation as per provision of section 149 and thus needs to be quashed.

The Judge held that it was sufficient if the notice under section 147 had been signed and issued by authority within time period and therefore delay in receiving the same would not provide any ground to quash the entire proceedings.

On writ appeal : HELD: In the instant case, the respondent reopened the assessment of the appellant for the assessment year 2011-12, through notice dated 31-3-2018 under section 148. Admittedly, the limitation period of six years for reopening the assessment, came to an end on 31-3-2018. The main plank of contention of the appellant is that the notice under section 148 dated 31-3-2018 has been received by the appellant through e-mail only on 18-4-2018 i.e., after the expiry of six years from the end of the assessment year under consideration and hence, the same is clearly barred by limitation, whereas the department contended that mere signing of notice by the respondent on 31-3-2018 amounts to issuance of notice under section 149 and therefore, the same is within the limitation period. [Para 8]

It is clear from the provision of section 149 that the maximum time limit for issuance of notice under section 148 for reopening the assessment is six years from the end of the relevant assessment year. In the instant case, the relevant assessment year is 2011-12; the limitation of six years for initiation of reassessment proceedings expired on 31-3-2018; and notice under section 148 signed by the respondent was dated 31-3-2018. In such circumstances, this court is required to examine that such notice is in adherence to the compliance of section 149 for reassessment proceedings. [Para 9]

While the appellant stated that notice under section 148 was received by her through e-mail only on 18-4-2018 and hence, the same is clearly barred by limitation, it is stated on the side of the department that notice under section 148 was signed by the respondent on 31-3-2018 and the same was given to the process server to be served on the appellant on the same day, but it was returned on 6-4-2018 stating that there was no such person in the given address. After ascertaining her address from the last return of income filed by her, the said notice was sent to the appellant's registered mail ID, which was also served on 18-4-2018. Thus, according to the respondent, the reassessment proceedings commenced from the moment, when the notice was signed by the respondent on 31-3-2018 and hence, the same is well within limitation. [Para 10]

It is apparent that the issuance of notice under section 149 is complete only when the same is issued in the manner as prescribed under section 282 read with rule 127 prescribing the mode of service of notice under the Act. The signing of notice would not amount to issuance of notice as contemplated under section 149. In other words, the requirement of issuance of notice under section 149 is not mere signing of the notice under section 148, but is sent to the proper person within the end of the relevant assessment year. [Para 12]

Concededly, the notice dated 31-3-2018 issued by the respondent was served on the appellant through mail, only on 18-4-2018. Though the respondent produced the relevant pages of notice server book maintained by the department to show that the notice of the respondent dated 31-3-2018 under section 148 is within the limitation period, but the same only disclosed that the notice dated 31-3-2018 was returned on 6-4-2018.

In instant case, there is no document made available to prove that the notice under section 148 dated 31-3-2018 was sent for despatch to the appellant, within the end of the relevant assessment year i.e., 31-3-2018. Thus, it is crystal clear that the notice under section 148 for reopening the assessment was not sent to the appellant, within the time stipulated under section 149 and hence, the same vitiates the reassessment proceedings initiated under section 147. [Para 13]

In such view of the matter, the order of the Judge as well as the notice issued by the respondent are liable to be set aside. As a sequitur, the writ appeal stands allowed. [Para 14]

FACT: A search under section 132 was conducted in the premises of the assessee-company. As a sequel to the search, a block assessment order on 29-11-2000.

A search under section 132 was conducted in the premises of the assessee-company. Consequent to the search a block assessment order was passed on 29-11-2000. The Commissioner (Appeals) quashed block assessment but at same time issued a direction under section 150 to the Assessing Officer for re-opening the assessment for the assessment year 1999-2000 (falling in the block period). In due compliance of the direction of the Commissioner (Appeals) the Assessing Officer issued a notice under section 148 on 25-4-2007 (after expiry of more that 6 years from date of block assessment order). Against order of Commissioner (Appeals), both revenue and assessee preferred appeals before the Tribunal. The Tribunal vide its order dated 11-7-2008 upheld quashing of block assessment order but also quashed direction issued under section 150. On other hand, the assessee preferred a writ petition against issuance of notice under section 148. The High Court quashing said notice ordered for issuance of fresh notice under section 148. Accordingly a fresh notice was issued and on assessment order under section 147 was passed (in 2008). On appeal by the assessee the Commissioner (Appeals) quashed the assessment order under section 147 on ground that direction of Commissioner (Appeals), in pursuance of which notice under section 148 was issued was already quashed by Tribunal, which had attained finality.

Against the order of the Commissioner (Appeals), the revenue had preferred instant appeal.

On appeal by revenue :

HELD: The case as put forth by the revenue was that the Commissioner (Appeals) had erred in quashing the order by holding that the re-assessment order passed under section 147 read with section 148 dated 30-12-2008 was invalid. The contention of the revenue was that the Tribunal's decision dated 11-7-2008 for block period from 1-4-1990 to 3-11-2000 had not become final and the High Court vide its order had granted liberty to the revenue to issue fresh notice if they wanted to do so and hence, the issue regarding validity of notice under section 148 pending with the subordinate judicial authorities was merged with the order of the High Court and as such fresh notice under section 148 dated 8-1-2008 issued by the Assessing Officer was in accordance with law. On the other hand, the assessee had submitted that the Commissioner (Appeals) had correctly quashed the notice in question as the notice was clearly time barred as per the provisions of the Act. [Para 4]

Thus, the view taken by the Assessing Officer, regarding the adjustment of the losses brought forward from the assessment year 1993-94, against the profits of the said unit for the assessment year under appeal was unassailable and no two views were possible. It could be rectified, provided section 154 would otherwise permit it. [Para 7] The contention of the assessee that reassessment having been completed only on 17-5-2002, the date which the demand notice bore, was barred by limitation, could not be accepted. The Assessing Officer has to serve a demand notice on the assessee under section 156 only if any tax, etc., is payable in consequence of any order passed under the Act. It was not denied that reassessment order passed on 28-3-2002 did not raise any demand of tax. The Assessing Officer was, therefore, not liable to serve any demand notice upon the assessee pursuant to the reassessment order. The issue of the demand notice on 17-5-2002 was unnecessary and had to be ignored as superfluous. [Para 8]

The argument, that the assessee could not challenge the ‘nil’ demand order made by the Assessing Officer, could not be appreciated. Even if no demand is created, but the assessee feels aggrieved by the reassessment order, then it is open to it to file an appeal and challenge the correctness of the order. [Para 9]

However, the contention of the assessee, that the notice under section 148 had been issued beyond the period prescribed, had force and was required to be accepted. The reasons recorded in the notice showed that there was no allegation that income chargeable to tax had escaped assessment because of the failure of the assessee to disclose fully and truly all material facts. On the contrary, the assessee had disclosed the dividend income and interest income in the profit and loss account and was alleged to have claimed deduction thereon under section 80-I in respect of the ‘A’ unit. That was only a legal position taken by the assessee after furnishing all the material facts. It is open to the assessee to put forth a legal contention or claim after furnishing all the material particulars. The assessee cannot be shut out from doing so. He cannot be said to have furnished untrue particulars or incomplete particulars for having raised a legal plea. The inference from the facts is for the Assessing Officer to draw. The duty of the assessee, even under the proviso to section 147, extends only to the furnishing of all the material facts. It is not for him to advice the Assessing Officer as to what inference should be drawn therefrom. The assessee, having filed the basic facts, may raise his own inference therefrom and put forth the same to the Assessing Officer which the Assessing Officer may, in his wisdom, accept or reject. But rejection of the assessee’s inference from the material facts cannot be equated with furnishing of untrue or incomplete particulars necessary for the assessment. In that view of the matter, the assessment order passed on 28-3-2002 was invalid, the notice under section 148 having been issued beyond the period of limitation, prescribed under the proviso to section 147. It is now well-settled that the issue of a valid notice under section 148 is a condition precedent for the validity of the reassessment. Therefore, the assessee was right in saying that the limitation for rectification under section 154 should be reckoned from the date of the original assessment order passed on 29-11-1996. In that case, the 4 years period expired on 31-3-2001. The order under section 154 having been passed on 28-2-2003 was barred by limitation and, hence, invalid. [Para 10]

HEADNOTE: Section  149,  read with sections  148  and  148A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment – Time limit for issuance of notice (TOLA) - Assessment year  2017-18  - Assessee filed writ petition challenging reassessment notice dated 30.06.2022 issued under section 148 for Assessment year  2017-18  as invalid and time barred - Earlier, AO had issued a notice under section 148 on 11.06.2021, which was to be treated as a notice under section 148A(b) as per Supreme Court directions in Ashish Agarwal - AO supplied information on 17.05.2022, and assessee replied on 30.05.2022 - AO then passed an order under section 148A(d) and issued a fresh notice under section 148 on 30.06.2022 - Whether considering limitation under Act read with TOLA and Supreme Court directions, last permissible date to issue notice under section 148 was 18.06.2022 - Held, yes - Whether therefore, impugned notice dated 30.06.2022 was invalid and liable to be quashed - Held, yes [Paras 7 to 9] [In favour of assessee]

FACT: ■

The assessee filed a writ petition under Article 226 challenging the reassessment notice dated 30.06.2022 issued under section 148 for AY 2017-18 as invalid and time barred. The respondents were the AO and the Income Tax Department.

■

The AO had earlier issued a notice under section 148 on 11.06.2021 for AY 2017-18 during the extended period under TOLA. Pursuant to the Supreme Court directions in Ashish Agarwal, the said notice was to be treated as a notice under section 148A(b). The AO supplied information on 17.05.2022, allowing 15 days to respond, making the reply due on 01.06.2022. The petitioner submitted its reply on 30.05.2022. The AO thereafter passed an order under section 148A(d) and issued a fresh notice under section 148 on 30.06.2022.

■

Considering the limitation under the Act read with TOLA and the Supreme Court directions, the last permissible date to issue the notice under section 148 was 18.06.2022.

■

On writ petition before the High Court.

HELD: ■

In the facts of the case, the respondent assessing officer has provided information pursuant to the directions issued by the Apex court in the case of Union of india v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64 /286 taxman 183 / 444 ITR 1 (sc) on 17.05.2022 and therefore, considering 15 days' time to file reply by the assessee, the due date would be 01.06.2022. The petitioner filed reply on 30.05.2022. The order under section 148A(d) as well as notice under section 148 was issued on 30.06.2022. However, considering the period of limitation from the date of issuance of notice under section 148 read with TOLA upto 30.06.2021, the limitation for issuance of notice under section 148 applying the decisions of apex court in the case of Union of India v. Ashish agarwal (Supra) as well as Union of India v. Rajeev bansal, [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70 / 301 taxman 238 (sc), would be 18.06.2022. [para 7]

■

Senior standing counsel Mr.yajnik has verified the above dates and could not controvert the same. [para 8]

■

In view of above, the impugned notice dated 30.06.2022 issued under section 148 would be invalid notice as the said notice is issued after 18.06.2022 as per the decision of Apex court in the case of Union of india v. Ashish agarwal (supra). Therefore, the impugned notice having been issued beyond the 'surviving time' would be invalid notice as held by the apex court in the case of union of india v. Rajeev bansal (supra). [para 9]

■

in view of foregoing reasons, impugned notice dated 30.06.2022 is hereby quashed and set aside and all consequential proceedings are also quashed and set aside. [para 10]

HEADNOTE: Section  149,  read with sections  147  and  148, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 / Section  282,  read with sections  279  and  280  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 – Income escaping assessment – Time limit for issuance of notice (TOLA) - Assessment year  2015-16  - Pursuant to survey under section 133A in case of Babylon Group, reassessment proceedings were initiated against assessee on allegation of cash receipt of Rs. 1 crore from sale of immovable property - AO issued notice under section 148 on 30-6-2021 and thereafter, pursuant to decision in Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64 (SC)/[2022] 286 Taxman 183 (SC)/[2022] 444 ITR 1 (SC) , issued fresh notice under section 148 on 26-7-2023 under new regime - Whether for assessment year 2015-16, notices issued under section 148 on or after 1-4-2021 were liable to be dropped as they would not fall for completion within period prescribed under TOLA - Held, yes - Whether therefore, notice issued under section 148 dated 26-7-2023 and consequential reassessment proceedings were liable to be quashed - Held, yes [Paras 11 and 13] [In favour of assessee]

FACT: ■

The assessee, an individual, filed return of income for AY 2015-16 on 30-06-2016 declaring income of about Rs. 7 lakhs. A survey under section 133A was conducted on 30-05-2017 in case of Babylon Group engaged in hotel business, during which a hard disk impounded from premises of Hotel Babylon Continental, Raipur, revealed huge cash transactions relating to investment in hotel project and sale/purchase of immovable properties during FYs 2013-14 to 2016-17. On examination of extracted data, the AO noted that the assessee, being one of sellers of immovable property, had allegedly received cash of Rs. 1 crore during FY 2014-15 which was not reflected in his books of account, though receipts through banking channels were reflected. The AO accordingly recorded reasons and reopened assessment for AY 2015-16.

■

The AO issued notice under section 148 on 30-06-2021 under old regime. Pursuant to decision of Supreme Court in Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64 (SC)/[2022] 286 Taxman 183 (SC)/[2022] 444 ITR 1 (SC), the AO issued notice under section 148A(b) on 21-5-2022, passed order under section 148A(d) on 25-7-2023 and thereafter issued fresh notice under section 148 on 26-7-2023 under new regime. The reassessment was completed under section 147 read with section 144B by making addition of Rs. 1 crore under section 69A.

■

On appeal, the CIT(A)/NFAC upheld validity of reassessment proceedings and sustained addition made under section 69A.

■

On appeal to the Tribunal.

HELD: ■

It is an admitted fact that the assessee filed his return of income on 30-6-2016. A survey action under section 133A was carried out on 30-5-2017 in the case of Babylon Group who are engaged in hotel sector. The Assessing Officer, after recording reasons, reopened the assessment and accordingly issued notice under section 148 on 30-6-2021. Subsequently on the basis of decision of Supreme Court in the case of Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal (supra), the Assessing Officer issued notice under section 148A(b) on 21-5-2022. After considering the reply of the assessee the Assessing Officer passed an order under section 148A(d) on 25-7-2023 and issued notice under section 148 on 26-7-2023 under the new regime. Thereafter, the Assessing Officer completed the assessment under section 147 read with section 144B wherein he made addition of Rs.1.00 crore under section 69A. The CIT(A)/NFAC upheld the re-assessment proceedings as well addition on merit. Under these circumstances, the issue for determination is whether the notice issued under section 148 for the assessment year 2015-16 on 26-7-2023 is a valid notice or not. [Para 10]

■
