Thus, for a notice to be validly issued for reassessment under section 148, the Respondent-Revenue would need to be compliant with section 151A, which has been interpreted and analysed in detail by a Division Bench of this Court in the case of Hexaware Technologies Ltd. v. Asstt.CIT [2024] 162 taxmann.com 225/464 ITR 430. [Para 4]

■ There is yet another facet of the matter which also flows from the judgment rendered in the case of Hexaware Technologies Ltd.(supra), namely whether the notice issued under section 148 in the instant case is barred by limitation under section 149. In Hexaware Technologies Ltd.(supra), this was framed as issue No.2 and was empathetically answered by stating that the deadline for issuing a notice under section 148 must be considered by applying the provisions of section 149 at the time of issuance of the notice. Therefore, the version of section 149 as it stood at the time of issuance of the notice under section 148 must be examined. In the instant case, the notice under section 148 was issued on 19 April, 2014. By this time, the time limit for issuance of the notice as stipulated under section 149 had expired, i.e., three year period under section 149 expired on 31 March, 2021. Therefore, on this ground too, the re-assessment proceedings had called for interference. [Para 5]

■

In the instant case, the notice for re-opening, the assessment for returns for the Assessment Year 2017-18 had been issued more than after six years of the end of the relevant assessment year. The re-opening is purported to be on the basis of information available on the Revenue’s insight portal which is essentially based on the thesis of allegedly bogus artificial passing capital gains arising out of trading in the script of M/s. Frontline Business Solution Ltd. The six years period expired on 31 March, 2024 while the three year period expired on 31 March, 2021. In the result, on this ground too, the Petition deserves to be allowed. [Para 6]

■

In the present case, it is apparent that the Respondent-Revenue has not complied with the Scheme notified by the Central Government pursuant to section 151A(2) . The Scheme has also been tabled in Parliament and is in the character of subordinate legislation, which governs the conduct of proceedings under section 148A as well as section 148 . In view of the explicit declaration of the law in Hexaware Technologies Ltd.(supra), the grievance of the Petitioner-Assessee insofar as it relates to an invalid issuance of a notice is sustainable and consequently, the very manner in which the proceedings have been initiated, vitiates the proceedings. [Para 7]

■

Counsel for both the parties agree that the proceedings initiated under section 148 would not be sustainable in view of the judgment rendered in Hexaware. The assessee has also drawn attention to a recent decision of this Court in Nainraj Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. v. Dy.CIT [2024] 165 taxmann.com 674 whereby in similar circumstances, this Court has allowed the petition considering the provisions of section 151A. [Para 8]

■

The Petitioner has also drawn attention to the decision of this Court in Kairos Properties Pvt. Ltd. v. Asstt.CIT [2024] 165 taxmann.com 760 . where the Court considered the effect of scheme as notified by the Central Government under the notification dated 29 March, 2022. The Court, considering the relevant provisions, has held that this scheme as notified in paragraph 3 of the notification would take within its ambit steps taken by the Revenue in issuing notice under section 148A(b) as also an order passed under Section 148A(d), so as to be included within the ambit of Section 151A. In this view of the matter, on both applicability of the law as laid down by this Court in Hexaware Technologies Ltd (supra) as also considering the observations of this Court in Kairos Properties Pvt. Ltd. (supra), the petition would be required to be allowed. [Para 9]

■

In the light of the above discussion, and as there is no dispute that the JAO had no jurisdiction to issue the impugned notice, the Writ Petition is accordingly allowed in terms of prayer. [Para 10]

HEADNOTE: I. Section  149,  read with sections  147  and  148, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section  3  of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Time limit for issuance of notice (Illustrations)  - Assessment year  2015-16  - Assessee filed its return of income - Based on a departmental enquiry alleging coordinated and premeditated trades in illiquid BSE stock options leading to non-genuine profit/loss, reasons to believe were recorded and a notice under old regime Section 148 was issued on 21-6-2021 - Since this notice was issued under erstwhile regime of re-assessment as provided under section 148 read with section 147 which had undergone total revamp by Finance Act 2021, Assessing Officer passed an order under section 148A(d), dated 30-7-2022 recommending reopening of case under section 148 - Subsequently, a notice under section 148 was issued on 30-7-2022 - Whether since notice under section 148 was issued under new regime on 30-07 - 2022, which fell beyond period of six years from end of relevant assessment year 2015-16, such notice was barred by limitation and hence, bad in law, liable to be quashed, and consequently, resultant reassessment proceeding as well as reassessment order were also bad in law - Held, yes [Para 7] [In favour of assessee]

FACT: ■

The assessee was a non-resident who filed his revised return of income.

■

Based on the enquiry conducted by the Department, it was noticed that assessee had entered into equity derivative transactions through coordinated and premeditated trading in illiquid stock options on the Bombay Stock Exchange. It was alleged that these transactions were manipulated and fabricated by a group of people in a coordinated manner so as to derive non-genuine and fictitious profit/loss in these illiquid derivative transactions. Based on this enquiry, it was observed that assessee had undertaken such transactions and hence a case was made of escapement of income from assessment.

■

The AO issued notice under section 148 on 21-06-2021 (old regime). Post Finance Act, 2021, the AO issued notices under section 148A(b) on 25-05-2022 and 20-06-2022, passed an order under section 148A(d) on 30-07-2022, and issued a fresh notice under section 148 on 30-07-2022. Statutory notices followed and assessment was completed under section 147 read with section 144C.

■

On appeal, the Commissioner (Appeals) quashed the notice issued under section 148 and held the reassessment proceedings as well as the reassessment order as bad in law.

■

On appeal to the Tribunal:

HELD: ■

Notice under section 148 is issued on 30-7-2022, which according to the assessee is barred by limitation, since it has been issued after expiry of 6 years from the end of the relevant assessment year i.e., assessment year 2015-16. According to the assessee, it is contrary to the mandate of the first proviso below section 149(1)(b) and therefore is invalid, bad in law and leading the impugned assessment proceedings as well as the impugned assessment order bad in law, liable to be quashed ab initio. [Para 6.1]

■

Identical issue had come up before the Coordinate Bench of ITAT, Mumbai in the case of Praful Arjun Rane v. ITO (IT Appeal No.1046 (MUM) of 2025, dated 30-9-2025), with the undersigned Accountant Member as the author. Detailed discussion is made in respect of applicable provisions on the issue in the present appeal as well as all the relevant judicial precedents have been discussed whereby the notice issued u/s.148 under the new regime was held to be barred by limitation and was thus, quashed resulting in the reassessment proceedings as well as the reassessment order as bad in law. [Para 6.2]

Section 148, read with section 147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Notice of - Assessment years 1971-72 and 1972-73 - Whether, where a valid notice under section 148 had been issued but no assessment had been completed nor were proceedings dropped by the Assessing Officer, he was disentitled to initiate fresh assessment proceedings by issuing another notice under section 148 - Held, yes - Whether assessment completed on the basis of second notice under section 148 would be invalid - Held, yes - Whether, where assessment proceedings initiated on the basis of first notice under section 148 got barred by limitation, they could be revived by issuing fresh notice under section 148 - Held, no

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Period of limitation) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Reassessment proceedings for year 2008-09 were initiated on 23-3-2015 after taking requisite approval of Jt. Commissioner - However on 18-1-2016, Assessing Officer issued another notice to assessee under section 148 for same year - Since proceedings initiated in pursuance of second notice were clearly time-barred, revenue took a stand that second notice should be taken as in continuation of first notice - It was found that second notice did not state anywhere that it was in continuation of earlier notice and fresh initiation did not have approval of Addl. Commissioner - Moreover, no satisfactory explanation was forthcoming as to why first notice issued by Assessing Officer under section 148 was not carried to its logical end - Whether, on facts, all these legal infirmities would lead to inevitable invalidation of all proceedings that took place pursuant to both notices - Held, yes [Paras 18-25] [In favour of assessee]IT: Where reassessment initiated vide two notices and second notice was beyond prescribed period and first notice proceeding were not continued and nowhere it was stated that second notice was in continuation of first one, reassessment was invalid

II. Section 148, read with sections 142(1) and 147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for - Assessment year 1997-98 - For assessment year 1997-98, Assessing Officer, on 24-8-1998, issued notice to assessee under section 142(1) - Assessee filed his return on 16-2-2000 - As return filed by assessee was beyond time limit prescribed under section 139(4), i.e., on or before 31-3-1999, Assessing Officer initiated reassessment proceedings against assessee under section 147 and completed assessment - Whether since in instant case revenue had not issued any notice under section 142(1) before end of assessment year and return furnished by assessee under section 139(4) on 16-2-2000 had been filed beyond time-limit prescribed under section 139(4) and was invalid return, in such circumstances, notice under section 148 had to be issued when an assessment, reassessment or recomputation was to be made under section 147 to tax income which had escaped assessment - Held, yes - Whether therefore, assessment completed without issuing notice under section 148 was invalid and bad in law - Held, yes

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Period of limitation) - Whether where impugned reassessment notice under section 148 had been issued beyond period of limitation after expiry of relevant assessment year, impugned notice and consequential notices were to be quashed and set aside - Held, yes [Paras 2 and 3] [In favour of assessee]

Section 143, read with  section 147/148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Assessment - Issue of notice (Notice u/s 143(2)) - Assessing Officer picked up assessee's return for scrutiny assessment and issued notice under section 148 - Assessee informed that revised return filed under section 139(5) was to be considered as return filed in response to notice under section 148 - Thereafter, Assessing Officer, without issuing notice under section 143(2) passed reassessment order under section 148 - Later, a notice under section 143(2) was issued but after expiry of limitation period prescribed for issuance of such notice - Whether reassessment notice under section 148 as well as order pursuant to said notice was to be quashed - Held, yes [Para 16] [In favour of assessee]IT : Where Assessing Officer picked up assessee's return for scrutiny and without issuing notice under section 143(2) passed reassessment order under section 148, and thereafter, a notice under section 143(2) was issued but after expiry of limitation period for issuance of such notice, reassessment order was to be quashed

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Period of limitation) - Whether where impugned reassessment notice under section 148 had been issued beyond period of limitation after expiry of relevant assessment year, impugned notice and consequential notices were to be quashed and set aside - Held, yes [Paras 2 and 3] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : Where impugned reassessment notice under section 148 had been issued beyond period of limitation after expiry of relevant assessment year, impugned notice and consequential notices were to be quashed and set aside

Section 148A, read with sections 148 and 149, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section  3 of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 - Income escaping assessment - Conducting inquiry, providing opportunity before issue of notice (Reassessment) - Assessment year 2013-14 - Whether validity of a notice issued under section 148 must be judged on basis of law existing on date on which such notice is issued - Held, yes - Whether a notice under section 148 cannot be issued in order to reopen assessment of an assessee in a case where right to reopen assessment was already barred under pre-amended Act on date when new legislation came into force - Held, yes - Whether applicability of section 149 is to be seen qua notice under section 148 and not with respect to notice issued under section 148A(b) or order passed under section 148A(b), and thus a notice, which had become time barred prior to 1-4-2021 as per the then prevailing provisions, would not be revived by virtue of application of section 149(1)(b) effective from 1-4-2021 - Held, yes - Whether therefore, where limitation under Act (erstwhile section 149) for reopening assessment for assessment year 2013-14 expired on 31-3-2020, notice issued in June 2021 in case of assessee was barred by limitation, hence, reassessment proceedings initiated pursuant to judgment in judgment in Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1 (SC) will also be regarded as beyond time limit - Held, yes - Whether further, since limitation under erstwhile section 149 for reopening assessment for assessment year 2013-14 expired on 31-3-2020, therefore, CBDT Notification No. 20/2021 which covers only those cases where 31-3-2021 was end date would not apply to facts of present case and even relate back theory of revenue could not safeguard reassessment proceedings initiated after 1-4-2021 - Held, yes - Whether therefore, section 148 notice dated 28-7-2022 issued pursuant to Judgment in Ashish Agarwal (supra) was to be quashed and set aside - Held, yes [Paras 20, 31 and 35 to 38] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : Where limitation under Act (erstwhile section 149) for reopening assessment for assessment year 2013-14 expired on 31-3-2020, notice issued in June 2021 in case of assessee was barred by limitation, hence, section 148 notice dated 28-7-2022 issued pursuant to Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1 (SC) was to be quashed and set aside as it was invalid, without jurisdiction and barred by limitation

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for - Assessment years 1994-95 to 1996-97 - Whether if a proper notice is issued but not served on assessee or if it is found that notice is not at all issued, then it cannot be stated that Assessing Officer assumed jurisdiction for making reassessment validly- Held, yes - When assessee received notice under section 142(1) requiring it to furnish information relating to reassessment to be done by Assessing Officer, it came to know that notice under section 148 dated 30-3-2001 was issued to it and same was allegedly served on it on 28-4-2001 - Assessee’s case was that no valid notice was served on it as signature of recipient from some ‘V’ although resembled with name of managing director of company ‘VK’ but that was not actual signature of ‘VK’; limitation period of issuing notice under section 148 for assessment year in question was to expire on 31-3-2001 and since department had not issued any notice by 31-3-2001 and by realizing its mistake, Assessing Officer made out a notice dated 30-3-2001 and took stand that it had been served by a notice server on 28-4-2001 - Assessing Officer, however, completed reassessment - Whether since there was no evidence for issuance of notice and signature of ‘V’ was not verifiable, it could be said that Assessing Officer made out notice on 30-3-2001 only to save his wrong action - Held, yes - Whether since proper service of notice was not done by Assessing Officer, assessment proceedings conducted consequent thereon were invalid - Held, yes

Section 153(2)(b) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Time limit for completion - Assessments for assessment years 1970-71, 1971-72 and 1972-73 reopened by notices under section 148 served on 22-7-1974 - 11mb limit for their completion expired on 21-7-1975, 31-3-1976 and 31-3-1977, respectively - ITO issued notices under section 142(1) in October 1978 for production of documents - Whether reassessment proceedings valid and could be continued beyond expiry of limitation period - Held, on facts, no

Section 148, read with section 139(4), of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Notice for - Assessment year 1987-88 - Return due on 31-7-1987 was not filed by assessee even till 25-10-1988 when notice under section 148 was issued and return was eventually filed on 30-3-1989 and assessment under section 143(3) read with section 147 was completed on 22-8-1990 - Whether, since neither any assessment had been made nor any return had been filed before the issuance of notice under section 148, which, again, was well within limitation period prescribed in section 149(1), said notice was valid - Held, yes

II. Section  149, read with section  148, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment -  Time limit for issuance of notice (Reassessment) - Assessment years  2013-14, 2014-15, 2016-17 and 2017-18 - Assessing Officer for relevant assessment years issued notices under section 148 (old regime) between 1-4-2021 and 30-6-2021 - Assessing Officer issued show cause notice under section 148A(b) - Thereafter, Assessing Officer, after considering replies furnished by petitioner, passed order under section 148A(d) along with notices issued under section 148 under new regime between July, 2022 and September, 2022 - Petitioner challenged validity of said notices on ground that same were barred by limitation - It was noted that for assessment years 2013-14, 2014-15, 2016-17 and 2017-18, date of notice under section 148 under TOLA were 17-6-2021, 9-06-2021, 30-06-2021 and 30-06-2021 and date of order under section 148A(d) and notice under section 148 were 29-7-2022, 27-7-2022, 30-7-2022 and 19-7-2022 respectively - However, last date for issuance of notice under section 148 as per surviving time were 22-6-2022, 27-6-2022, 14-6-2022 and 18-6-2022 respectively - Whether since impugned notices under section 148 were issued beyond period of 'surviving time' as per direction of Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/301 Taxman 238/469 ITR 46 (SC), such notices would be invalid - Held, yes [Para 68] [In favour of assessee]

Section 148, read with sections 149 and 153(2), of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for - Assessment years 1995-96 to 1999-2000 and 2001-02 - Whether where Assessing Officer issued notice, to assessee under section 148 after expiry of 4 years from end of relevant assessment years, and further had not mentioned amount of escaped income, in such circumstances, it could be said that, notice under section 148 was beyond limitation provided under section 149(1)(a) - Held, yes -Whether where assessment order was passed after expiry of one year from end of financial year in which notice under section 148 was served upon assessee, reassessment would also be time-barred under section 153(2) - Held, yes

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Notice for - Assessment year 1984-85 - Whether simply preparing notice under section 148 but keeping it on file past limitation period does not tantamount to issuing same, and, thus, such notice is bad in law - Held, yes

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Period of limitation) - High Court by impugned order held that where impugned reassessment notice under section 148 had been issued beyond period of limitation after expiry of relevant assessment year, impugned notice and consequential notices were to be quashed and set aside - Whether SLP filed by revenue against impugned order was to be dismissed, however, question of law was to be kept open - Held, yes [Paras 4 and 5] [In favour of assessee]

Section  148,  read with sections  147,  144  and  144B, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Issue of notice for  (Limitation) - Assessment year  2015-16  - Whether notice under section 148 issued on 23-4-2022 for assessment year 2015-16, being issued after 1-4-2021, was beyond limitation and therefore without jurisdiction - Held, yes - Whether consequently reassessment order, demand notice, penalty notices/orders and recovery notices were to be quashed - Held, yes [Paras 6 and 11] [In favour of assessee]

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Period of limitation) - High Court by impugned order held that where impugned reassessment notice under section 148 had been issued beyond period of limitation after expiry of relevant assessment year, impugned notice and consequential notices were to be quashed and set aside - Whether SLP filed by revenue against impugned order was to be dismissed, however, question of law was to be kept open - Held, yes [Paras 4 and 5] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : SLP dismissed against impugned order of High Court that where impugned reassessment notice under section 148 had been issued beyond period of limitation after expiry of relevant assessment year, impugned notice and consequential notices were to be quashed and set aside

Section 148, read with section 292BB, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Service of notice) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether where notice for reopening of assessment was issued to assessee after expiry of period of limitation at old address of assessee which had already been changed by assessee in official record by updating PAN data base, it could be said that there was no service of reassessment notice upon assessee - Held, yes - Whether, further, service of notice to Chartered Accountant of assessee was not service at all and merely because assessee had participated in reassessment proceedings by filing return and filing objection to reassessment, notice issued to it through its Chartered Accountant, to sought reasons to believe, same could not make service of notice valid - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, reassessment proceedings on assessee was bad in law and deserved to be quashed - Held, yes [Paras 25 and 45] [In favour of assessee]IT : Where reassessment notice under section 148(1) was issued against assessee after expiry of period of limitation at old address of assessee which was already changed by assessee before date of issuance of said reassessment notice in official record by updating PAN data base, it could be said that there was no service of reassessment notice upon assessee

Section 148A, read with sections 148 and 149, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section  3 of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 - Income escaping assessment - Conducting inquiry, providing opportunity before issue of notice (Reassessment) - Assessment year 2013-14 - Whether validity of a notice issued under section 148 must be judged on basis of law existing on date on which such notice is issued - Held, yes - Whether a notice under section 148 cannot be issued in order to reopen assessment of an assessee in a case where right to reopen assessment was already barred under pre-amended Act on date when new legislation came into force - Held, yes - Whether applicability of section 149 is to be seen qua notice under section 148 and not with respect to notice issued under section 148A(b) or order passed under section 148A(b), and thus a notice, which had become time barred prior to 1-4-2021 as per the then prevailing provisions, would not be revived by virtue of application of section 149(1)(b) effective from 1-4-2021 - Held, yes - Whether therefore, where limitation under Act (erstwhile section 149) for reopening assessment for assessment year 2013-14 expired on 31-3-2020, notice issued in June 2021 in case of assessee was barred by limitation, hence, reassessment proceedings initiated pursuant to judgment in judgment in Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1 (SC) will also be regarded as beyond time limit - Held, yes - Whether further, since limitation under erstwhile section 149 for reopening assessment for assessment year 2013-14 expired on 31-3-2020, therefore, CBDT Notification No. 20/2021 which covers only those cases where 31-3-2021 was end date would not apply to facts of present case and even relate back theory of revenue could not safeguard reassessment proceedings initiated after 1-4-2021 - Held, yes - Whether therefore, section 148 notice dated 28-7-2022 issued pursuant to Judgment in Ashish Agarwal (supra) was to be quashed and set aside - Held, yes [Paras 20, 31 and 35 to 38] [In favour of assessee]   Circulars and Notifications: Notification No. S.O. 1432(E) [No.20/2021/F.No.370142/35/2020-TPL] dated 31-3-2021, Notifications No. 20 of 2021 dated 31-3-2021 and No. 38 of 2021 dated 27-4-2021

I. Section 153, read with  sections 147, 148 and 149, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Time-limit for completion of - Assessment years 2001-02 to 2004-05 - Whether term 'issue' appearing in section 149 cannot mean as 'issue and serve' - Held, yes - Whether jurisdiction becomes vested in Assessing Officer to assess/reassess escaped income at moment notice under section 148 is issued; service under Act is not a condition precedent to conferment of jurisdiction on Assessing Officer but a condition precedent only to making of order of assessment - Held, yes - Whether where reassessment proceedings initiated under section 147 are not concluded to a logical end, Assessing Officer cannot issue fresh reassessment notice under section 148 - Held, yes - For relevant assessment years, Assessing Officer had issued notices under section 148 on 23-9-2005 - He again issued notices for assessment year 2001-02 on 25-9-2006 after getting necessary sanction from Additional Commissioner - After receipt of affidavit on 10-11-2006 he again issued notices under section 148 on 24-11-2006 for assessment years 2001-02 to 2004-05 - Assessment orders were passed on 24-12-2007 - Whether assessments for assessment years 2001-02 to 2004-05 framed with reference to notice issued under section 148 on 24-11-2006 during pendency of assessment were bad in law - Held, yes - Whether further assessments were to be completed by 31-12-2006 with reference to notices issued on 23-9-2005 and, therefore, assessments completed on 24-12-2007 were also barred by limitation - Held, yes

Section 148, read with section 149, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Period of limitation) - Whether where impugned reassessment notice under section 148 had been issued beyond limitation period of six years after end of assessment year in question, impugned notice and consequential orders/notices if any were to be quashed and set aside - Held, yes [Paras 3 and 4] [In favour of assessee]

Section 149, read with sections 148 and 148A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 / Section 282, read with sections 280 and 281 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 – Income escaping assessment – Time limit for issuance of notice (Reassessment proceedings) - Assessment year 2015-16 - Assessee, an individual, did not file return for A.Y. 2015-16 - Based on information of cash deposits of about Rs. 1.42 crores, time deposits of Rs. 13 lakhs, and interest income of about Rs. 3.29 lakhs, a notice under Section 148A(b) was issued on 26.03.2022 - An order under Section 148A(d) recording satisfaction for reopening and a notice under Section 148 were both issued on 18.04.2022 - Subsequently, faceless reassessment proceedings culminated in an ex parte order under Sections 147 r/w 144 and 144B dated 18.03.2024 determining tax of about Rs. 53.44 lakhs, with a penalty under Section 271(1)(c) of an equivalent amount and attachment of bank accounts - Whether since order passed under section 148A(d) and notice issued under section 148 of Act were 4 days beyond period of limitation, impugned notice issued under section 148 and consequent order of assessment were to be quashed - Held, yes [Paras 21 and 24] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX: Where assessee was issued notice under section 148 for cash and time deposits, since order passed under section 148A(d) and notice issued under section 148 were 4 days beyond period of limitation, impugned notice and satisfaction order beyond limitation period rendered reassessment notice and order invalid and both were quashed.  INCOME TAX: Where assessee, a non-filer for relevant year, was subjected to reassessment by notices under amended regime of sections 148, 148A, and 149, since revenue did not invoke or rely upon TOLA for extension or saving limitation period, reassessment could not be quashed based solely on concession recorded in Rajeev Bansal decision.

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for - Assessment year 1993-94 - Whether when a valid return is already on record, action under section 148 without framing assessment under section 143(3) can be held a valid action - Held, no - Assessing Officer processed return of income filed by assessee under section 143(1)(a) on 31-3-1994 and issued intimation to assessee - Thereafter, ADI passed on 20-4-1994 certain information about assessee to Assessing Officer - Though Assessing Officer was having time to issue notice under section 143(2) up to 28-2-1995, but he did not issue notice and instead issued notice to assessee under section 148 on 28-11-1994 and thereafter passed order under section 144 read with section 148 on 31-3-1997 - Whether by issuing notice under section 148 Assessing Officer had illegally transgressed jurisdiction to complete assessment on 31-3-1997 - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, assessment order passed on 31-3-1997 was barred by limitation - Held, yes - Whether otherwise also issue of notice under section 148 was illegal and invalid - Held, yes

Section 143 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Assessment - Issue of notice - Assessment year 1997-98 - Whether proviso to section 143(2) applies to a return filed in response to notice issued under section 148 - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, where Assessing Officer issued notice under section 143(2) beyond a period of one year from date of filing of return in response to notice under section 148, said notice was invalid and, thus, assessment proceedings initiated in pursuance of it were to be set aside - Held, yes [In favour of assessee]

Section 148, read with sections 147 and 154, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice (Pending rectification proceedings) - Assessment year 1995-96 - Assessment proceedings reopened under section 148 were quashed and set aside by Tribunal by holding that since proceedings under section 154 initiated against assessee were pending, no reopening proceedings under section 147/148 could have been issued/initiated - On appeal by revenue, High Court allowed appeal and remanded matter to Tribunal by observing that as proceedings under section 154 were beyond period of limitation prescribed under section 154(7), said notice was invalid and therefore, reopening proceedings under section 147/148 would be maintainable - It was found that proceedings under section 154 were not subject-matter before High Court and there was nothing on record that notice under section 154 was withdrawn on ground that same was beyond period of limitation prescribed under section 154(7) - Whether therefore, proceedings initiated under section 154 could be said to have been pending and Tribunal was right in holding that it was not permissible for revenue to initiate reassessment proceedings under section 147/148 - Held, yes - Whether therefore, impugned order of High Court was to be quashed and set aside and order of Tribunal was to be restored - Held, yes [Paras 4 to 6] [In favour of assessee]

I. Section  69,  read with sections  147,  148  and   148A , of the Income-tax Act, 1961 / Section  103,  read with sections  279  and  280  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 – Unexplained investments (Reassessment) – Assessment year  2015-16  – Whether reassessment proceedings initiated pursuant to notice under section 148 dated 12-4-2022 for AY 2015-16 were barred by limitation and liable to be quashed – Held, yes – Whether further, where Assessing Officer issued notice under section 148 without verifying registered Deed of Apartment and earlier registered Agreement for Sale and proceeded mechanically without application of mind, notice under section 148 and consequent reassessment order were bad in law and void ab initio – Held, yes [Paras 3, 4 and 6.3] [In favour of assessee]

Section  149, read with section  147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment -  Time limit for issue of notice (Reassessment) - Assessment year  2015-16 - Assessee filed return of income on 17-9-2015 - Based on information received under Risk Management Strategy of CBDT, notice under section 148 was issued on 23-6-2021 after obtaining prior approval of PCIT - Reassessment was completed under section 147 read with section 144B, disallowing short-term capital loss under section 94(7) - Assessee challenged reassessment on ground that subsequent notice issued under section 148 on 29-7-2022 was barred by limitation under amended provisions read with applicable judicial principles - It was noted that limitation period available to Assessing Officer for issuance of notice under section 148, as per section 149, was expired on 31-3-2022, however, notice under section 148 was issued on 29-7-2022 - Whether reassessment proceedings initiated beyond prescribed limitation period were void ab initio and unsustainable in law - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, impugned reassessment proceedings initiated under section 148 vide notice dated 29-7-2022 are barred by limitation and deserve to be quashed and consequently, reassessment order passed under section 147 read with section 144B also deserved to be quashed - Held, yes [Paras 5.1, 5.2 & 6] [In favour of assessee]

Section 148, read with section 149, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Period of limitation) - Whether where impugned reassessment notice under section 148 had been issued beyond limitation period of six years after end of assessment year in question, impugned notice and consequential orders/notices if any were to be quashed and set aside - Held, yes [Paras 3 and 4] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : Where impugned reassessment notice under section 148 had been issued beyond limitation period of six years after end of assessment year in question, impugned notice and consequential orders/notices were to be quashed and set aside

Section 143 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Assessment - Issue of notice (Limitation) - Assessment year 2007-08 - Notice under section 143(2) was issued to assessee on 18-8-2008 by Dy. CIT, Circle 3 who had no jurisdiction over assessee's case - Realising that mistake, Dy. CIT, Circle 3 transferred file to ITO Ward 3 who had jurisdiction over assessee's case and thereafter, on 26-8-2009, fresh notice under section 143(2) was issued to assessee - Whether since Dy. CIT, Circle 3 had no jurisdiction over assessee's case, notice issued by him/her was invalid and without jurisdiction and had to be treated as non est in eye of law - Held, yes - Whether valid notice issued by ITO, Ward-3 was dated 26-8-2009 which was clearly barred by limitation and assessment order framed consequent to this notice would also become invalid and barred by limitation - Held, yes [Para 4.2] [In favour of assessee]IT : Assessment order framed consequent to notice issued under section 143(2) which was time-barred, would also become invalid and time-barred

Section 153(2) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Limitation - Whether on facts stated under head ‘Reassessment - Notice for’, since notice issued under section 148 on 25-10-1988 was a valid notice, assessment made on its basis on 22-8-1990 was well within limitation of section 153 (2) - Held, yes

Section 148, read with sections 149 and 151, of the Income tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Whether prescribed period of limitation for reassessment is to be reckoned from end of relevant assessment year and not financial year - Held, yes - Whether word ‘issued’ in section 149 is required to carry meaning of expression ‘issued and served’ within prescribed period of limitation - Held, yes - Whether, where notice under section 148 for assessment year 1975-76 was admittedly served on assessee on 30-3-1984, assessment proceedings initiated on basis of such notice were hit by section 149 - Held, no

Section 149, read with section 150, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Time limit for completion of re-assessment - Assessment year 1999-2000 - Whether period of limitation as provided under section 149 will always be available and even direction given under section 150 cannot enlarge scope of limitation - Held, yes - A block assessment order, pertaining to block period 1.4.1990 to 3.11.2000, was passed in 2000 - Commissioner (Appeals) quashed said order but issued a direction under section 150(1) to reopen assessment for assessment year 1999-2000 - In pursuance of such direction a notice under section 148 was issued on 25.5.2007 (after expiry of more than six years) - Two parallel proceedings were commenced, one before Tribunal against order of Commissioner (Appeals), and another before High Court against 148 notice - Tribunal quashed direction under section 150(1) on ground that Commissioner (Appeals) was not empowered to give direction to Assessing Officer to re-assess completed assessment after expiry of limitation - On other hand High Court quashed notice under section 148 and permitted issuance of fresh notice - In 2008, a fresh notice under section 148 was issued and in consequence thereof, an assessment order under section 147 was passed - On appeal by assessee, Commissioner (Appeals) quashed assessment order under section 147 by following order of Tribunal in which direction of Commissioner (Appeals) under section 150(1) was quashed - Whether when a particular direction had been quashed by Tribunal such a direction no longer survived - Held, yes - Whether further since order of High Court giving permission to issue fresh notice under section 148 was subject to section 149, it could not have enlarged scope of limitation as provided under section 149 - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, action of Commissioner (Appeals) was to be approved - Held, yes [In favour of assessee]

I. Section  149,  read with sections  147  and  148, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section  3  of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Time limit for issuance of notice (Illustrations)  - Assessment year  2015-16  - Assessee filed its return of income - Based on a departmental enquiry alleging coordinated and premeditated trades in illiquid BSE stock options leading to non-genuine profit/loss, reasons to believe were recorded and a notice under old regime Section 148 was issued on 21-6-2021 - Since this notice was issued under erstwhile regime of re-assessment as provided under section 148 read with section 147 which had undergone total revamp by Finance Act 2021, Assessing Officer passed an order under section 148A(d), dated 30-7-2022 recommending reopening of case under section 148 - Subsequently, a notice under section 148 was issued on 30-7-2022 - Whether since notice under section 148 was issued under new regime on 30-07 - 2022, which fell beyond period of six years from end of relevant assessment year 2015-16, such notice was barred by limitation and hence, bad in law, liable to be quashed, and consequently, resultant reassessment proceeding as well as reassessment order were also bad in law - Held, yes [Para 7] [In favour of assessee]

Section 147, read with  section 254, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 [Corresponding to section 34, read with section 31, of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922] - Income escaping assessment - Time Limit for Issue of Notice - Assessment years 1949-50 and 1950-51 - Assessee was a shareholder of a company - For relevant assessment years, ITO applied provisions of section 23A of 1922 Act to company on 25-6-1956 - ITO also initiated proceedings against assessee under section 34 of 1922 Act without issue of any notice - On appeal, AAC cancelled reassessment with direction to redo it up to 31-3-1961 though it was within knowledge of AAC that by date on which he disposed of appeal, time stipulated in section 34 of 1922 Act for commencement of proceedings under that section, had expired - Accordingly, ITO issued notice under section 34 of 1922 Act on 27-10-1956 and completed reassessment on 11-2-1957 - Whether, on facts, direction issued by AAC travelled far beyond scope of powers conferred under section 31 of 1922 Act - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, reassessment completed on 11-2-1957 being beyond period of limitation was invalid - Held, yes

Section  148, read with section  149, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment -  Issue of notice for (Limitation) - Assessment year  2009-10 - Reassessment proceedings were initiated in case of assessee by issuing notice on 15-3-2016 by Assessing Officer - Assessee filed writ petition on ground that on 13-04-2016, for first time, he was served with notice under section 148(1) through his Chartered Accountant and he was never served with notice alleged to be issued under section 148(1) on 15-03-2016 and, thus, no notice was issued within period of limitation as prescribed under section 149(1)(b) read with section 148(1) and, therefore, initiation of proceeding for reassessment was barred by limitation - Single Judge allowed writ petition holding that no notice was served to assessee under section 148(1) and service of notice to Chartered Accountant was not service at all - Whether had it been a case of revenue that notice was served upon assessee before 31-03-2016, then why they have again issued notice through Chartered Accountant on 13-04-2016 was not understood and, therefore, notice under section 148 issued on 13-04-2016 was after period of limitation which was dated 31-03-2016 - Held, yes - Whether Single Judge had not committed any illegality, irregularity or jurisdictional error in impugned order warranting interference by High Court - Held, yes [Paras 13 and 14] [In favour of assessee]

Section 153(1)(c), read with sections 148 and 139, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Time limit for completion of - Assessment year 1979-80 - Assessee filed return in response to notice under section 148 - It later filed a revised return on 30-3-1988, which was processed and assessment was finally completed on 15-3-1989 - Whether, where section 148(1) clearly lays down that notice issued under section 148 shall be deemed to be one issued under section 139(2) and, therefore, all provisions of Act including those of sections 139(5) and 153(1)(c) shall apply accordingly, no sooner returns got filed on 30-3-1988 in terms of section 139(5), Assessing Officer statutorily got benefit of extension of time for making assessment by one more year from said date in accordance with provisions of section 153(1)(c) and order of Commissioner (Appeals) annulling said assessment on ground of limitation had to be reversed - Held, yes

Section 148, read with sections 147 and 154, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice (Pending rectification proceedings) - Assessment year 1995-96 - Assessment proceedings reopened under section 148 were quashed and set aside by Tribunal by holding that since proceedings under section 154 initiated against assessee were pending, no reopening proceedings under section 147/148 could have been issued/initiated - On appeal by revenue, High Court allowed appeal and remanded matter to Tribunal by observing that as proceedings under section 154 were beyond period of limitation prescribed under section 154(7), said notice was invalid and therefore, reopening proceedings under section 147/148 would be maintainable - It was found that proceedings under section 154 were not subject-matter before High Court and there was nothing on record that notice under section 154 was withdrawn on ground that same was beyond period of limitation prescribed under section 154(7) - Whether therefore, proceedings initiated under section 154 could be said to have been pending and Tribunal was right in holding that it was not permissible for revenue to initiate reassessment proceedings under section 147/148 - Held, yes - Whether therefore, impugned order of High Court was to be quashed and set aside and order of Tribunal was to be restored - Held, yes [Paras 4 to 6] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : During pendency of proceedings under section 154, it was not permissible for revenue to initiate reassessment proceedings under section 147/148

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Notice of - Assessment year 1961-62 - Whether issuance of notice within period of limitation gives jurisdiction to Assessing Officer to proceed to make reassessment irrespective of whether or not it is served within period of limitation - Held, yes

Section 149, read with section 148, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Time-Limit for issuance of notice [Escaped income in excess of Rs. one lakh] - Assessment years 1999-2000 and 2000-01 - For relevant assessment years, Assessing Officer sought to initiate reassessment proceedings taking a view that assessee had made payments in cash in excess of Rs. 20,000 and, thus, 20 per cent of said payments was to be disallowed - Assessee challenged initiation of reassessment proceedings contending that notice under section 148 was issued after expiry of prescribed period - It was apparent from records that escaped assessment was more than Rs. one lakh and notice had been issued within a period of six years from end of relevant assessment years - Whether on facts, impugned notice was issued within period of limitation as prescribed under clause (b) of section 149(1) and, thus, reassessment proceedings could not be quashed on ground of limitation - Held, yes [In favour of revenue]IT: Where it was apparent from records that escaped assessment was more than Rs. One lakh and notice under section 148 had been issued within a period of six years from end of relevant assessment years, in view of provisions of clause (b) of section 149(1), notice so issued could not be quashed on ground of limitation

I. Section 149, read with sections, 148 and 148A, of Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Time limit for issuance of notice (Applicability of) - Assessment year 2015-16 - Assessee filed its return of income on 30-11-2015 - Original scrutiny assessment under section 143(3) was completed on 28-6-2017 - A notice under section 148 was issued on 20.04.2021 - Pursuant to order of Supreme Court in case of Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1 (SC), said notice dated 20.04.2021 was deemed to be a show cause notice under section 148A(b) for which another one was issued on 30.05.2022 - Thereafter, provisions of section 148A(d) were complied with by passing an order, dated 25-7-2022 and issuing a notice under section 148 of same date - Assessee contended that notice so issued under section 148 was barred by limitation - Whether since notice issued under section 148 was dated 25-7-2022, a period of six years expired on 31-3-2022, and thus, impugned notice was barred by limitation - Held, yes - Whether, accordingly, notice so issued and assessment completed thereafter under section 147 were liable to be quashed - Held, yes [Paras 3.5 and 4] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : Where pursuant to order of Supreme Court in case of Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1 (SC), a reopening notice under section 148 was issued upon assessee for assessment year 2015-16 on 25-7-2022, since a period of six years expired on 31-3-2022, impugned notice was without jurisdiction and barred by limitation  INCOME TAX : Where reopening notice was issued upon assessee on ground that further, amount of foreseeable losses was not an item to be added to book profit under provisions of section 115JB, and further, amount of foreseeable losses was not an item to be added to book profit under provisions of section 115JB, since said addition was not in form of any asset, reopening of assessment was not valid  INCOME TAX : Where assessee, engaged in business of civil, mining, marine and engineering and construction activities, made provision for foreseeable losses, since assessee following mercantile system of accounting had made said claim in accordance with AS-7 issued by ICAI, impugned provision for foreseeable losses was to be allowed  INCOME TAX : Where Assessing Officer disallowed contingency expenses on basis that same were not recorded in books of accounts but however, Commissioner (Appeals) restricted said addition to adhoc 2.5 percent of contingency expenses, since Coordinate Bench in case of sister concern of assessee had deleted entire ad hoc addition of 2.5% sustained by Commissioner (Appeals), following rule of consistency, addition so sustained by Commissioner (Appeals) during year was to be deleted as well  INCOME TAX : Where reassessment proceedings were initiated and concluded by passing impugned order wherein addition was made towards management consultancy fees paid by assessee to an entity, however, Commissioner (Appeals) deleted addition, in absence of department coming in appeal before Tribunal, exercise of reopening case and making reassessment stood vitiated

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 [Corresponding to section 34 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922] - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for - Assessment years 1946-47 to 1949-50 - Assessee-HUF filed its return for relevant assessment years on 18-11-1950 - As ITO had rejected claim under section 25A of 1922 Act and declined to hold that parent HUF had suffered partition, he took no action upon return filed by assessee - But after order of Tribunal dated 28-10-1954 in appeals filed by parent HUF, ITO issued notice for reassessment on 4-3-1955 - Though assessee filed returns pursuant to said notice yet it assailed notice on ground that it was invalid inasmuch as assessee had already filed returns relating to those years on 18-11-1950 - ITO however rejected claim of assessee and made reassessment - Whether, on facts, impugned notices issued by ITO under section 34 of 1922 Act were barred by limitation and consequently, assessment orders passed in pursuance of said notices were invalid - Held, yes

Section 148, read with sections 143 and 144B, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Notice under section 143(2)) - Assessment year 2015-16 - Assessee challenged reassessment order on ground that notice issued under section 143(2) was issued beyond prescribed time limit and, thus, was time-barred– It was observed that return in response to notice under section 148 was filed by assessee on 31-3-2021, and notice under section 143(2) was issued on 20-11-2021 which in accordance with applicable provisions of proviso to sub-clause (ii) of section 143(2) was to be issued within 3 months i.e., on or before 30-6-2021 - Whether, therefore, notice under section 143(2) being issued beyond prescribed time was barred by limitation and consequently, impugned reassessment order, dehors a valid notice under section 143(2) was to be quashed - Held, yes [Para 18] [In favour of assessee]

Section 153, read with sections 147(b) and 148, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Time limit for completion of - Whether law of limitation prevailing at time of passing of order, and not law at time of notice, would be applicable - Held, yes - Whether where notice under section 148 was issued on 31-3-1988 but assessment was completed on 31-3-1991, it being beyond two years of notice, in view of amendment to section 153(2) with effect from 1-4-1989, assessment was invalid as being time barred - Held, yes
Circulars and notifications - CBDT Circular No. 549, dated 31-10-1989

Section  149, read with section  148, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment -  Time limit for issuance of notice (Reassessment) - Assessment year  2013-14 - Whether entire process under section 148A(a) to (d) and issuance of notice under section 148 has to be completed within total time available in terms of section 149(1) for issuance of notice - Held, yes - Assessee filed return of income for assessment year 2013-14 - Assessment was completed under section 143(3) - On 29-6-2021, notice under unamended section 148 was issued, which was later treated as a deemed notice under section 148A(b) - Assessing Officer issued final notice under section 148 on 29-7-2022 after supplying reasons and materials and completing process under section 148A - Whether after accounting for permissible exclusions under substituted section 149, time available to complete reassessment process had expired on 23-7-2022 - Held, yes - Whether since notice under section 148 was issued beyond said time, same was barred by limitation and, thus, reassessment proceedings and consequential assessment order were to be quashed - Held, yes [Paras 16 to 21] [In favour of assessee]

Section 149, read with section 147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Time limit for issuance of notice - Assessment year 1988-89 - Assessee-company started its business as per licence issued by Excise Department and in order to obtain licence, partners of firm contri-buted capital on 28-3-1988 - Assessing Officer made an addition while completing assessment for assessment year 1989-90 - Tribunal deleted addition made by Assessing Officer, holding that genuineness of investment could be considered only in assessment year 1988-89, because same fell outside purview of accounting period relevant to assessment year 1989-90 - There-after Assessing Officer, on basis of order of Tribunal, issued notice under section 148 on 21-2-2001 for reopening assessment for assessment year 1988-89 and completed assessment treating capital contributed by partners as unexplained - Whether since Tribunal nowhere in its earlier order had given any direction to Assessing Officer to reopen assessment for assessment year 1988-89, assessment could not be said to be reopened as per directions of Tribunal - Held, yes - Whether since notice was issued under section 148 upon assessee after six years from end of relevant assessment year 1988-89, same was beyond time and barred by period of limitation and, therefore, assessment completed by Assessing Officer by issue of notice under section 148 was without jurisdiction and void ab initio - Held, yes

Section 154, read with section 80-I, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Rectification of mistakes - Apparent from record - Assessment year 1994-95 - Assessment on assessee was first made on 29-11-1996 under section 143(3) - Later, assessment was reopened and reassess-
ment was completed on 28-3-2002 - However, no fresh demand was raised pursuant thereto - Thereafter, Assessing Officer, by order 
 dated 28-2-2003, rectified assessment consequent upon passing of order under section 154 on 10-2-2003 for assessment year 1993-94 on ground that computation of assessee’s ‘A’ unit’s income for that year had resulted in a loss, which had to be carried forward and adjusted against profit of said unit for year in question under section 80-I (6) - Assessee challenged rectification order, inter alia, on grounds that issue sought to be rectified was a debatable one; and that reassessment order passed on 28-3-2002, being without jurisdiction, time-limit for rectification would start from original assessment order on 29-11-1996 and, therefore, rectification order was barred by limitation - Whether in terms of provisions of section 80-I(6), view taken by Assessing Officer regarding adjustment of losses brought forward from assessment year 1993-94 against profits of said unit for assessment year under appeal was unassailable and, therefore, assessment could be rectified, provided section 154 otherwise permitted it - Held, yes - Whether however, since reassessment order passed on 28-3-2002 was invalid, notice under section 148 having been issued beyond period of limitation prescribed under proviso to section 147, limitation of four years for rectification under section 154 should be reckoned from date of original assessment order passed on 29-11-1996 and in that case, order under section 154 having been passed on 28-3-2002 was barred by limitation and, hence, invalid - Held, yes

Section 149 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Period of limitation - ITO, a while initiating reassessment proceedings under sections 147 and 148, sent notice which was signed on 30-3-1970 and was issued on 31-3-1970, to assessee - Notice was admittedly served on her in first week of April 1970 - Assessee contended that notice though issued within prescribed time limit was not served within limitation period and was, therefore, illegal and without jurisdiction - ITO, however, made best judgment assessment under section 144 and also imposed penalty under section 271(1)(a) - Tribunal annulled both reassessment and penalty proceedings by accepting aforementioned contention of assessee - Whether limitation provision of section 149 envisaged only issuance of notice to assessee and not its actual service on him and, therefore, reassessment proceedings and resultant penalty proceedings were wrongly annulled by Tribunal - Held, yes

Section  149,  read with sections  147  and  148, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 /  Section  282 ,    read with  sections  279   and   280    of the Income-tax Act, 2025, and section  3  of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 – Income escaping assessment – Time limit for issuance of notice (Surviving-time computation) – Assessment year  2013-14  – Assessing Officer issued notice under section 148 on 7-6-2021 under pre-amended regime – Thereafter, following procedure under amended reassessment regime, Assessing Officer issued fresh notice under section 148 on 24-7-2022 and completed reassessment under section 147 read with section 144B – Assessee contended that notice dated 24-7-2022 was barred by limitation on basis of surviving-time computation after COVID-19 relaxations – Whether, since as per Supreme Court ruling in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/301 Taxman 238/469 ITR 46 (SC), revenue had 24 days to issue notice under new regime, i.e. up to 1-7-2022, notice issued on 24-7-2022 was beyond limitation period and, thus, barred by limitation – Held, yes – Whether consequently, notice issued under section 148 on 24-7-2022 and reassessment order passed under section 147 read with section 144B were void ab initio and invalid – Held, yes [Para 7] [In favour of assessee]

Section  149,  read with sections  148  and  150  of the Income-tax Act, 1961/ Section  282,  read with sections  280  and  283  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 - Income escaping assessment – Time limit for issuance of notice (Remand) - Assessment year  2011-12  - Assessees, engaged in business of construction, development of township, housing projects and other realty projects, had shown work-in-progress and customer advances received/taken over from group entities/partners - Assessing Officer initiated reassessment proceedings under sections 147/148 pursuant to directions issued by Commissioner (Appeals) under section 150(2) and made additions under sections 69C and 68 towards unexplained expenditure, work-in-progress and customer advances -  Commissioner (Appeals) quashed reassessment proceedings holding that directions issued under section 150(2), forming basis for issuance of notice under section 148, had already been expunged by Tribunal in assessee-group cases and, in absence of such directions, notice issued under section 148 was barred by limitation prescribed under section 149  - It was noted that earlier order of Tribunal on identical facts had attained finality as Department had not filed any appeal against same - Whether, therefore, Commissioner (Appeals) was justified in holding reassessment proceedings and consequential assessment orders as void ab initio - Held, yes [Paras 7 and 7.2] [In favour of assessee]

Section  149,  read with sections  148  and  148A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment – Time limit for issuance of notice (TOLA) - Assessment year  2017-18  - Assessee filed writ petition challenging reassessment notice dated 30.06.2022 issued under section 148 for Assessment year  2017-18  as invalid and time barred - Earlier, AO had issued a notice under section 148 on 11.06.2021, which was to be treated as a notice under section 148A(b) as per Supreme Court directions in Ashish Agarwal - AO supplied information on 17.05.2022, and assessee replied on 30.05.2022 - AO then passed an order under section 148A(d) and issued a fresh notice under section 148 on 30.06.2022 - Whether considering limitation under Act read with TOLA and Supreme Court directions, last permissible date to issue notice under section 148 was 18.06.2022 - Held, yes - Whether therefore, impugned notice dated 30.06.2022 was invalid and liable to be quashed - Held, yes [Paras 7 to 9] [In favour of assessee]

facts.text:
For the assessment year 1966-67, assessment was reopened under section 148 by the ITO in the case of assessee, an individual. In the reassessment, the ITO included certain amount as unexplained investment in the income assessed earlier in the original assessment. The notice under section 148 was issued on 29-3-1975 but it was served on the assessee on 7-4-1975. On appeal before the AAC, the assessee contended that the notice having been served after the expiry of period of limitation, the reassessment proceedings were barred by limitation. The AAC rejected the assessee's contention. On second appeal, the Tribunal held that the notice under section 148 was not only to be issued but served within the period of limitation as laid down in section 149, and since the notice was served on the assessee after the expiry of 8 years, the order of reassessment was set aside.

On reference:

When the assessee received notice under section 142(1) requiring it to furnish information relating to the reassessment to be done by the Assessing Officer, it came to know that notice under section 148 dated 30-3-2001 was issued to it and same was allegedly served on it on 28-4-2001.The assessee brought to the notice of the Assessing Officer that no notice under section 148 had been served upon him and required the Assessing Officer to supply the notice and in response to this letter, notice issued under section 148 dated 30-3-2001, duly signed by some ‘V’ was provided to the assessee and thereafter the assessee participated in the assessment proceedings. During the assessment proceedings, the assessee’s case was that no valid notice was served on it as signature of the recipient from some ‘V’ although resembled with the name of the managing director ‘VK’ of the company but that was not actually signature of ‘VK’. The Assessing Officer, however, completed the reassessment. On appeal, the Commissioner (Appeals) upheld the reassessment order.

In second appeal, the assessee contended that limitation period of issuing notice under section 148 for the assessment year in question was to expire on 31-3-2001 and since the department had not issued any notice by 31-3-2001 and by realizing its mistake, the Assessing Officer made out a notice dated 30-3-2001 and took the stand that it had been served by a notice server on 28-4-2001; it was against preponderance of probability that a notice server could have taken 28 days to serve a notice, which was impractical, and revealed that the Assessing Officer only to cover his inaction for issuing of notice within time, made out a notice dated 30-3-2001 after the expiry date, i.e., 30-3-2001 and had just delivered the notice to someone and recorded signatures, namely ‘V’, which was not resembling with the signatures of ‘VK’, managing director of the company. The assessee further contended that requirement of section 148 was that notice should be issued; in its case, no evidence for issuance of notice, as such, had been produced by the department; in view of fact that without adducing any evidence of the issuance of notice, as such it was stated to have been served on 28th April after 28 days, it could well be assumed that said service of notice was an afterthought; and since there was no service of notice under section 148, the assessment made in pursuance of such notice was illegal and without jurisdiction.

For the assessment year 1997-98, the Assessing Officer, on 24-8-1998, issued notice to assessee under section 142(1). The assessee filed his return on 16-2-2000. As the return filed by assessee was beyond time-limit prescribed under section 139(4), i.e., on or before 31-3-1999, the Assessing Officer initiated reassessment proceedings against the assessee under section 147 and completed the assessment. The assessee filed the instant miscellaneous application and contended that no notice under section 148 was ever issued before passing the assessment order. Hence, the assessment under section 147 became invalid.

In the assessment years 2001-02 to 2004-05, the Assessing Officer had issued notices under section 148 after recording reasons on 23-9-2005. The Assessing Officer again issued notice for the assessment year 2001-02 on 25-9-2006 after getting necessary sanction from the Addl. Commissioner. After receipt of affidavit on 10-11-2006, he again issued notices under section 148 on 24-11-2006 for the assessment years 2001-02 to 2004-05.

The assessee challenged the said assessments before the Commissioner (Appeals) on assumption of jurisdiction under section 147 by the Assessing Officer.

According to the assessee, the assessments framed were bad in law on two counts. Firstly, the proceedings initiated during the pendency of the earlier assessment proceedings would be bad in law and the order passed would be invalid and liable to be quashed. Secondly, since the notices under section 148 for the assessment years 2000-01 to 2004-05 were issued on 23-9-2005, the assessments for those years were to be completed by 31-12-2006. However, the assessments had been framed on 24-12-2007. Hence, the assessments made by the Assessing Officer for the assessment years 2000-01 to 2004-05 were barred by limitation. The Commissioner (Appeals) dismissed the assessee's appeal.

The assessee filed appeal before the Tribunal where the revenue contended that the assessee had himself claimed that he never received notices dated 23-9-2005 and 25-9-2006, which, in fact, led to issue of notices dated 24-11-2006 and therefore, period of limitation should be counted from 24-11-2006. According to the revenue service of notice under section 148 is the foundation of jurisdiction of the assessing authority and, hence, the assessments could not be annulled on the ground that the same had become barred by limitation.

For initiating reassessment proceedings under sections 147 and 148, the ITO sent a notice for reassessment which was actually signed by him on 30-3-1970 but was admittedly issued by registered post on 31-3-1970 to the assessee. The assessee was actually served with the notice later in the first week of April 1970. She contended that the notice, though issued within the limitation period, had not been served within eight years from the end of the relevant assessment year and was, hence, illegal and without jurisdiction. The ITO rejected this contention and made a best judgment assessment under section 144. He also initiated penalty proceedings and imposed penalty under section 271(1)(a). The AAC rejected the assessee's appeals. On further appeal, the Tribunal purportedly, following the Supreme Court's judgment in the case of Banarsi Debi v. ITO [1964] 53 ITR 100, annulled the reassessment as also the penalty proceedings on the ground that a notice of reassessment issued against the assessee before the limitation date prescribed under section 149 but served on the assessee after such date would be without jurisdiction and, thus, void and inoperative.

On reference:

For the assessment year 1962-63, the assessment order was made on the actual receipt basis on 12-10-1966, but the AAC on 20-4-1967, decided that for the year 1961-62 though the assessment was made under "actual receipt basis" it should be done on the "due basis". On the basis of his order, the Assessing Officer issued notice dated 30-3-1971 under section 148 for the assessment year 1962-63.

On writ, the assessee contended that the purported notice under section 148 dated 30-3-1971, which was served upon him on the 1-4-1971, was barred by limitation and that the said notice for re-assessment for the relevant assessment year was issued in violation of section 149.

The petitioner also contended that the purported action of the respondent No. 1 in issuing the said notice was illegal, invalid and inoperative, inasmuch as the said notice had been issued without obtaining the necessary sanction of either the Commissioner or that of the Central Board of Direct Taxes, as required under section 151.

The assessee-firm filed original return of income for the assessment year 1981-82 on 31-8-1981 and for the assessment year 1982-83 on 1-9-1982. The assessment was completed under section 143 and the incomes declared in the returns were accepted. The Assessing Officer subse- quently received a complaint along with documentary evidences, sought necessary sanction from the Commissioner and upon receipt thereof the proceedings under section 147(a), read with section 148 of the Act were initiated and pursuant thereto notice dated 26-3-1991 was issued. In response to the notice, the assessee filed returns declaring incomes for both the assessment years. The Assessing Officer made reassessment for both the years on 29-3-1993. The assessee appealed to the Commissioner (Appeals) on ground that reopening of the assessment under section 148 was barred by limitation as the provisions of section 147(b) were applicable and not the provisions of section 147(a). The Commissioner (Appeals) rejected the assessee’s contention. On appeal to the Tribunal, the Tribunal held that notice being invalid, the reopening was not according to law and reassessments so framed were to be quashed.

On appeal under section 260A :

For the assessment year 1961-62, a notice under section 148 was issued and despatched on 24-2-1970. No return was filed in response thereto. Therefore, the Assessing Officer issued another notice on 10-10-1973 under section 142(1) intimating to the assessee to appear on 23-11-1973. The assessee filed a reply to this notice stating that the alleged notice under section 148 was not served upon him and no proceedings under section 148 could be maintained against him as notice was not served upon him within 8 years. However, on 13-5-1974, an assessment order under section 144 was passed. By filing writ petition the assessee challenged the reassessment order. The High Court held that notice issued before limitation, if served on the assessee after limitation, would be void and ineffective but since an appeal was pending against the order of assessment, the High Court directed that the appeal be decided by the appellate authority in accordance with law.

On appeal to the Supreme Court:

. The assessments of the assessee were made only to dispose of returns which had been filed by it. The assessment for the assessment year 1974-75 was made on 10-3-1977. The assessments for the assessment years 1975-76 to 1977-78 were completed on 30-1-197

8. For the assessment years 1978-79 and 1979-80, the assessee had not filed any returns on its own. The department being of the view that the re-union was not valid and as such, the bigger HUF could not be considered to have come into existence held that the properties thrown by P into the hotchpot of the bigger re-united family had continued in law to belong to the smaller HUF of P. The department, therefore, assessed the income of these properties in the hands of the smaller HUF of P for the assessment years 1971-72 and 1972-73. This was objected to by P. Ultimately, the matter went to the Hon’ble High Court in reference. The High Court decided the matter in the case of P by its judgment dated 13-4-1981. The High Court found that in the facts of the case, the essential ingredients of re-union had existed The High Court held that the re-union was valid. It, therefore, held that the department was in error in not assessing the income of the properties thrown by the smaller HUF of P into the common hotchpot of the re-united family. According to the High Court, the re-union being valid, these properties had come to belong to the re-united family and, hence, the income of those properties was assessable in the hands of the re-united family. Thereupon, on the basis of this decision of the High Court, the department proceeded under section 147 in the case of the re-united

family to assess the income that had escaped assessment. In the assessments that were completed, the department brought to tax in the hands of the re-united family the income of all the properties since, as per the decision of the High Court, all the properties had, on re-union, come to belong to the re-united family. Notices under section 148 in respect of all the assessment years were issued on 27-3-1982. On appeals, the Commissioner (Appeals) also upheld the ITO’s orders.

On second appeal, the assessee contended that the assessments should be struck down as being invalid. It was stated that assumption of jurisdiction under section 147 was not justified. It was also stated that the assessments made were bad in law on account of the fact that notices under section 148 were invalid, having been issued after the expiry of the time limit prescribed for the issue of such notices. It was pointed out that the issue of a notice under section 148 was a condition precedent to the validity of any assessment under section 147 and if the notice issued under section 148 was not valid, assessment was not legally sustainable. Another contention raised was that since the HUF had ceased to exist by the time the assessments came to be made, the assessments were bad in law, as law did not provide for making assessment on defunct HUF It was stated that the HUF had disrupted on 8-5-1972. HELD (AS PER THIRD MEMBER)

The issue before the Division Bench as could be seen from the order of the Commissioner (Appeals) itself is narrowed down as to the validity of the assessment made by the Assessing Officer under sections 143(3) and 147 in the light of the initiation of reassessment proceedings by issuance of notice. The provisions of sections 147 to 151 are specific provisions which enable the department to reassess any income that has escaped assessment. These provisions underwent significant changes with effect from 1-4-1989. In the light of these changes, each and every initiation of assessment proceedings made on or after 1-4-1989 must be governed by the amended provisions as held by the decision of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case of Rakesh Aggarwal v. Asstt. CIT [1997] 225 ITR 496 /[1996] 87 Taxman 306 . Under section 148(1), before making an assessment, reassessment and computation under section 147, the Assessing Officer is required to serve on the assessee a notice requiring him to furnish a return of income. Under section 148(2), the Assessing Officer, before issuing any notice under section 148(I), is required to record his reasons for doing so. The provisions relating to the time-limit for issuance of notice are set out in section 149. [Para 15]

A notice issued within the period prescribed under section 149, even though served thereafter, gives a perfectly valid initiation.
